In the name of Allah, the Most Gracious, the Most Merciful.

﴿A surah which We have sent down and made obligatory, and in which We have sent down clear signs, that you may remember.﴾ (1):

Its name is Surah al-Nur (The Light)(1). If we survey the subject matter named by, or entitled, Surah al-Nur, you will find light pervading all its sections. I do not say its verses, nor do I say its words, but light pervades all its letters. Why?

They said: Because "light" is among the words whose utterance indicates its meaning and which people know more than by any other definition. People know light merely by pronouncing this word. Light is not known except through the reality of what it accomplishes, which is that by which visible things become clear and by which existing things are made manifest. Were it not for this light, we would see nothing.

Thus light is known by its property: it is what gives you the ability to see visible things, as evidenced by the fact that if they are in darkness you do not see them. Therefore light itself is not seen, but by it we see things. Allah the Exalted is the Light of the heavens and the earth; He illuminates them for us, but we do not see Him, glory be to Him.

But are all things visible? Are there not audible, odorous and tasted things? They said: Yes, but the first proof of all these, and of the occurrence of events, is the visible, because all the proofs of the universe are visible; we see them first, then when you hear, when you smell, when you touch, and when you distinguish the heavy from the light, or the near from the far. All of this is a branch of what exists in you, after you believe that Allah, who brought you into being, is the One who brought into being for you everything. So when you look at light, you find that light is a sensory matter by which you see things.

In the past they used to believe that a person perceives things by a ray that issues from the eye, falling upon the object so that it is seen, until the Muslim scholar al-Hasan ibn al-Haytham came, nullified this theory, and said: the ray comes from the seen object to the eye, so that it is seen, and not the reverse. He proved this by the fact that if an object is in darkness we do not see it while we are in light; for if a ray were to issue from you, you would see it.

In the light of this theory we understand His saying, exalted is He: ﴿And We made the sign of the day to be a visible one...﴾ (12) [al-Isra]: it is "visible" (mubsira), because the ray comes from there, so it is as if it were the one that sees.

But what benefit does this sensory light have for man, the vicegerent on earth? When you see things, you deal with them in a way that gives you their good and keeps their evil away from you. Had you not seen things, you could not have dealt with them. Otherwise, how would you walk in a dark place where there is something that could harm you, such as snakes or broken glass?

Thus you cannot find the way to where your foot should go, or take the good of things and avoid their evil, except by sensory light. Likewise, if you walk in darkness and without guidance, you must collide with one stronger than you, who will crush you, or with one weaker than you, whom you will crush.

For this reason the Truth, blessed and exalted is He, named the method that guides you along the paths of life "light."

When the divine lordly light is absent, people make for themselves lights according to their capabilities and environments, beginning with the oil lamp and the kerosene lamp. People varied even in these, until the age of electricity, fluorescent lights, neon and other means of lighting in which people vary greatly. This is at night; but when the sun rises, everyone extinguishes their lights and lamps. Why? Because the lamp of Allah has appeared, and in it all are equal, none distinguished from another.

Likewise is the immaterial light, the light of the method that guides you if it bears Allah's direction. So extinguish the lamps of human direction; it is not proper for you to be illuminated by a light while your Lord's light is present. Rather, you must hasten and take what you are able of your Lord's light. Just as you took Allah's sensory light and thereby cancelled all other lights, so take Allah's light in values, take Allah's light in morals, in dealings and in conduct. This will make you independent of any light of human lights and their methods.

Do you not see Nimrod, how he was confounded when Ibrahim, peace be upon him, cut off his argument and drove him to the proof from which he could not escape, when he said to him: ﴿Indeed, Allah brings the sun from the east, so bring it from the west...﴾ (258) [al-Baqara].

And the Truth, blessed and exalted is He, pours forth from His lights and attributes of perfection upon His creatures whom He made His vicegerents on earth, so He said: ﴿Indeed, I am going to place upon the earth a successive authority (khalifa)...﴾ (30) [al-Baqara]. The vicegerent on earth is not one generation which Allah created and appointed on earth until the Hour; rather, the vicegerents are successive generations and progeny, one dying and another being born, in connected links of lineages, not of individual selves.

The vicegerent does not succeed in his vicegerency unless he proceeds in it according to the desire of the One who appointed him. The affliction of people in their vicegerency for Allah on earth is that they consider themselves originals, not vicegerents. The vicegerent always keeps this vicegerency in mind; therefore he looks to the origin and considers what the One who appointed him wants from him.

The Truth, blessed and exalted is He, appointed for Himself a vicegerent on earth so that the marks of His power and the attributes of His perfection would appear upon him. Allah is All-Powerful, Allah is All-Knowing, Allah is All-Wise, Allah is Self-Sufficient, Allah is Most Merciful, Allah is Most Forgiving, etc. He, glory be to Him, gives of His attributes and pours them upon His creatures and His vicegerent on His earth, some of these attributes: He gives you power from His power, mercy from His mercy, sufficiency from His self-sufficiency. Yet the attribute remains in His hand, glory be to Him; if He wills, He takes it away. Do you not see that the strong may become weak, and the rich may become poor?

This is so that we may know that these attributes are not intrinsic to us, and that these gifts are not originally ours; rather they are an outpouring from the outpouring of Allah and a gift from His gifts, glory be to Him. Therefore it is incumbent upon us to use them according to His desire, exalted is He. If your Lord gives you power, He has poured it upon you so that you may pour it upon others. He gave you knowledge so that you may scatter it among people; He gave you wealth so that you may safeguard the right of the poor.

So since Allah, exalted is He, has poured upon you of the attributes of perfection, and He Himself has retained ownership of these attributes, then if He wills He takes them from you. Therefore you must seize the opportunity and make use of the presence of this quality in you, making it fruitful in what Allah wants from you before it is taken away. So that when it is taken from you, it will reach you from others.

So give charity while you are wealthy, so that you may receive the charity of others if poverty befalls you; honour the orphan, so that someone will honour your orphan after you. If you meet the events of life with this outlook, your heart will be at peace, you will be safe from the calamities of time, and you will receive events with contentment. And how would you worry while you are in a society that cares for you as you cared for it, carries you as you carried it, and cooperates with you as you cooperated with it?

And Allah spoke truly when He said: ﴿And let those fear who, if they left behind them weak offspring, would be anxious for them. So let them fear Allah and speak words of appropriate justice.﴾ (9) [al-Nisa].

So: the Truth, blessed and exalted is He, wants from His vicegerent on earth that he be a gatherer of the attributes of perfection which make creation happy by the effects of the Creator in them, and this is the true vicegerency.

Surah al-Nur came to carry the light of values: the light of the immaterial, the light of values, the light of dealings, the light of morals, the light of management and conduct. And since Allah, exalted is He, has set this light for us, it is not proper for people to set for themselves other laws, because, as He, glory be to Him, said: ﴿And whoever Allah does not give light, for him there is no light.﴾ (40) [al-Nur]. For had this sun not existed, no one could have made light for himself at all.

The Truth, blessed and exalted is He, wants His vicegerent on earth to be pure, noble, honourable and dignified. Therefore He set for him laws that secure this goal, and the first and most important of these laws is the law of the lawful meeting of man and woman in a sound manner in broad daylight, so that this union produces pure offspring worthy of Allah's vicegerency on earth. For this reason, the first thing the Truth, glory be to Him, spoke of in this surah was the matter of adultery (zina).

It is remarkable that this surah comes after Surah al-Mu'minun, in whose beginning Allah said: ﴿Successful indeed are the believers.﴾ (1) [al-Mu'minun]. Then He mentioned of these successful believers: ﴿And those who guard their private parts.﴾ (5) [al-Mu'minun]. And here He said: ﴿The adulterous woman and the adulterous man...﴾ (2) [al-Nur], bringing in contrast those who guard their private parts.

From this we understand that a man and a woman do not meet except upon light from Allah and guidance from His wise law, because He, mighty and majestic, is the Creator of man, He knows best what suits him, He created his particles and knows how these particles harmonize with one another, and He, glory be to Him, created the faculties of the soul and knows how these faculties coexist without conflict.

Therefore, it is natural that if you want to produce a vicegerent in the universe contrary to Allah's desire and contrary to the characteristics of the Truth, the universe must be disordered and the faculties of the soul will clash within it. And what do you expect from this vicegerent if he comes in darkness? At that time there appear the diseases of offspring, from burying children alive to killing them even in the wombs of mothers, and a man may doubt his child, so he hates him, neglects him, and leaves him to wander.

Therefore this matter will not be set right except when the vicegerent comes in accordance with the characteristics of his Lord, and when the spouses unite according to what Allah has legislated in broad daylight, not when each creeps upon the other in the darkness of sin, so that what is forbidden happens, lineages become mixed, and the bond of society disintegrates.

Among the harshest experiences of life for a person is to doubt that his child is his, and to be gripped by this thought, so that he neglects his child, his own flesh and blood, spends here and there, and deprives him in a way contrary to pure lineage, where a father longs for his child, goes hungry so that he may feed him, and goes bare so that he may clothe him.

So the Truth, glory be to Him, wants offspring nurtured by two parents in a sound, lawful fatherhood and a sound, lawful motherhood, united upon the light of Allah.

You may draw a comparison between a woman who conceived through illicit intercourse and another who conceived a lawful, pure pregnancy. You will find the first bearing it reluctantly and with aversion, wishing to rid herself of it while it is a fetus in her womb; if she forces herself until its birth, she rids herself of it on the same night, even by abandoning it on the side of the road.

As for the woman with a lawful pregnancy, she yearns for the child, and if it is delayed for some time she becomes anxious, going between doctors; if Allah honours her with pregnancy, she flies with it in joy and pride, and guards it in her walking, her movements, her sleep and her standing until the delivery. She bears its pains willingly, then embraces it, nurses it, and lives her life in its service and care.

Allah wants His vicegerent on earth to come from pure union, openly before the eyes of all people and in the light of Allah's immaterial light. He wants the husband to come in through the door in the light of this illumination, not to sneak in the darkness through the servants' entrance.

Therefore the Truth, glory be to Him, threatens those who oppose this method and want to corrupt the honour of the vicegerency that Allah wants pure, defile lineages, inflame hearts with hatred and enmity, and sow doubt in the souls of creation. Crimes against honour do not limit their harm to personal enmities; rather they extend to harming society as a whole.

Look at AIDS, which now threatens societies, and which results from illicit intercourse. The danger of AIDS is not limited to its two parties; it extends to others. Therefore it is in the interest of the whole society that we enforce the punishment for fornication, so that this disease does not spread.

We are surprised at those who attack Allah's law regarding the hudud when it decrees stoning a married adulterer to death. Do these not know that we sacrifice one to preserve the safety of millions in health and well-being? Do they not see what happens, for instance, in the plague, which has defeated scientists until now and for which they have found no cure, and how the Shari'a commanded us that if the plague strikes a land we should not go to it, and commanded those within it not to leave it? Why? To confine this epidemic so that it does not spread among people.

The same applies to the matter of adultery, because the harm of the adulterer is not limited to himself alone; rather his harm extends to the whole society. With the observation that the Shari'a distinguishes between the married adulterer and the unmarried one, and likewise the adulteress: in the case of marriage, semen is multiplied in one place. Therefore we were asked in San Francisco: Why did you permit polygyny but did not permit polyandry? This was from them on the basis of analogizing the man to the woman: why does a woman not marry and combine four men?

I say:
1. Al-Qurtubi said in his tafsir (6/4693): "The purpose of this surah is to mention the rulings of chastity and concealment. And 'Umar, may Allah be pleased with him, wrote to the people of Kufa: Teach your women Surah al-Nur."

Then the Almighty speaks about the first matter among what He has enjoined upon His servants:

﴿The adulteress and the adulterer—flog each one of them with a hundred lashes. And let not pity for them detain you in the religion of Allah, if you should believe in Allah and the Last Day. And let a group of the believers witness their punishment.﴾ (24:2)

We have said: Almighty Allah addressed this matter out of concern for the safety of the offspring and the purity of this human being whom Allah made His vicegerent on earth. When we reflect on the Qur'anic context of this verse, we find that the word al-zani (the adulterer) indicates both the female and the male. In the language, the relative pronoun alladhi is for the singular masculine, allati for the singular feminine, alladhani for the dual masculine, allatani for the dual feminine, alladhina for the plural masculine, and allati/allata'i for the plural feminine.

However, there are nouns that cover all these forms, such as man (who/whoever), ma (what), and al (the definite article). You say: "The one who honored me came" (jaa man akramani), "The one [feminine] who honored me came" (jaat man akramtani), and "Those who honored me came" (jaa man akramuni).

Likewise, the (al) in (al-zani) indicates both the feminine and the masculine. Yet the Almighty explicitly mentioned both so as to remove what might arise among some people as disagreement over which of the two is the cause of this crime. This disagreement occurred even among the imams and jurists. Some say: the adulterer is the one who penetrates and acts, and the woman is the one penetrated; the act belongs to the man, not the woman, so he alone bears this responsibility.

Accordingly, Imam al-Shafi'i (may Allah be pleased with him) relates that a man came to the Prophet (ﷺ) and said: "O Messenger of Allah, I had intercourse (wataat) with my wife in Ramadan." The Prophet (ﷺ) said to him: "Expiate (kaffir)" (1).

Al-Shafi'i derived from this hadith that the expiation (kaffarah) is imposed upon the man and not the woman; otherwise the Messenger would have said to him: "Expiate" in the dual form.

But we must distinguish between wat' (penetration) and jima' (intercourse): wat' is the act of the man even if the wife is unwilling and refusing; whereas jima' is the state of consent and acceptance from both parties, and in this case the expiation is upon both of them together. Therefore, the Blessed and Exalted Allah explicitly mentioned "the adulterer and the adulteress" to remove this doubt and this disagreement.

I hold in this matter that the one who asked the Messenger of Allah was the man; had it been the woman, he would have said to her also: "Expiate." The ruling is specific to the one who asked.

And one who reflects on the verses of the prescribed punishments finds, for example, in the punishment for theft the saying of the Exalted: ﴿And the thief, male and female...﴾ (5:38), where He began with the masculine. But in the punishment for adultery He said: ﴿The adulteress and the adulterer...﴾ (24:2), where He began with the feminine. Why this difference in Qur'anic expression?

It is said: because the woman's role in the matter of adultery is greater and her entry into it is wider; she is the one who entices the man, excites him and stirs his emotions. Therefore Allah, Blessed and Exalted, commanded men to lower their gaze and commanded women not to display their adornment, so as to block the windows of this crime and prevent its causes.

As for theft, the burden of expenditure and the cost of living usually rests on the shoulders of the man; he is the one charged with it, so it is the man who steals. As for the woman, she usually receives in the home and it is not her task to provide the costs of living. Yet there is no objection to a woman also stealing; therefore the mention of theft began with the man.

Thus, by comparing the verses of the Qur'an you find the speech weighed with extreme precision; every word and every letter has its contribution. This is the speech of a Wise Lord, and if the matter were merely ordinary legislation, He would not have attended to such details.

Then comes the deterrent punishment for this crime: ﴿So flog each one of them with a hundred lashes...﴾ (24:2). "Flog" (ijlidu) is a command, but to whom? He did not say "O ruler" or "O judge," because the command here is addressed to the whole community (ummah); the establishment of the prescribed punishments is entrusted to the entire community. But can the whole community rise up together and carry out one act in every place?

It is said: the community is like the public prosecutor to the governor; it must choose whom it deems fit for the office to carry out what it wills. Whoever appoints a judge has judged. Given this, beware of appointing to judgment one who is not fit for it, for the responsibility will then be upon you if he wrongs or oppresses. So the waw and alif in ﴿fa-jlidu﴾ (24:2) indicate great meanings: the community as a whole cannot flog every adulterer or adulteress, but when it gives its allegiance to its imam, and chooses him to establish the limits of Allah, it is as if it were itself the one who established the punishments and carried them out.

Therefore the Prophet (ﷺ) said: "Whoever appoints anyone to a matter while among the people there is someone better than him, he will not smell the fragrance of Paradise" (2).

Why? Because when you put in charge of people's affairs one who is not fit for them while there are those who are fit, you spread corruption in society. And do not think you can hide anything from people's eyes; they have such awareness and attentiveness that they distinguish the competent from others. If they stay silent and overlook it, they will ask behind your back: why did he appoint this one and leave the one more capable than him? He must have other qualifications; he entered through the back door. Why do we not do the same? Then chaos reigns, rights are lost, frustration, idleness and lethargy spread, disorder occurs in society and interests are disrupted.

Yet despite all this, we cannot blame the ruler when he chooses one who is not fit before we blame ourselves first. We are the ones who chose him and deceived in the allegiance to him, so Allah empowered him over us to deceive in his choice too. But if each of us performed his duty in choosing one who is fit, no one who deceives the people would have reached the ranks of leadership, and matters would be set right, and a person would draw near to office through work, diligence, sincerity, trustworthiness, truthfulness and devotion to serving society.

Among the mercies of Allah toward creation is that He casts sincerity and love of work into some hearts and plants compassion for creatures within them. Therefore in every office or every bureau you see a humble official who loves people and is eager to settle their affairs; you see him wearing thick glasses through which he sees with difficulty, always bent over papers and files, and people come to him to settle their affairs: "O so-and-so Effendi, give me such-and-such, and write me such-and-such." Allah has expanded his breast toward people, so he turns no one away.

All these matters we understand from the waw and alif in ﴿fa-jlidu...﴾ (24:2). As for jald, it means striking: we say "jalada-hu," meaning he struck his skin; "ra's-ahu," meaning he struck his head; "zahr-ahu," meaning he struck his back. And jald is striking in a particular manner, such that it neither cuts flesh nor breaks bone; for a blow varies according to its force and the instrument used to strike. Among blows there is one that breaks bone without cutting skin, another that cuts skin without breaking bone, and another that causes pain short of either.

Then He, Glorified, says: ﴿And let not pity for them detain you in the religion of Allah...﴾ (24:2): a warning against foolish mercy, mercy in the wrong place, in accordance with the words of the poet: "So be harsh that they may be restrained, and whoever is resolute, let him sometimes be harsh toward the one he pities."

Pity has no place within the limits of Allah. Show pity to them in your private matters among yourselves. It is strange that you abandon pity in matters of the prescribed punishments while on the other hand you strike and steal people's wealth, violate their sanctities, and stir up sedition and wars among them. Where then is pity?

So there is no room for mercy or pity within the limits of Allah. We are not more merciful to creation than the Creator. The limits were not laid down out of love for tormenting people; they were laid down and made stringent so as to prevent falling into the crime that calls for the prescribed punishment. The cutting off of one hand prevents the cutting off of thousands of hands.

As for those who accuse Islam of harshness and brutality in applying the prescribed punishments, have they forgotten what they did at Hiroshima, whose effects remain until now? Have they forgotten the wars they ignite throughout the world, which reap thousands of lives? Is that the foolish mercy that has no meaning? Or is it hatred of the limits of Allah?

We recall from the past that a military guard accompanied the pilgrim caravan to protect the pilgrims from highwaymen, and that this pilgrimage convoy was called (al-mahmal). When Saudi Arabia established the rule of Allah and applied the prescribed punishments, the roads became secure, and people became independent of these guards despite their vastness, the branching of their routes, their roughness among the mountains, valleys and vast deserts, which no human eye can govern or guard; they need the legislation of the Mighty, Majestic Creator.

Yet when they counted the hands that had been cut off, they found them very few, and most of them from outside the Kingdom. I recall that I once said in the sermon of 'Arafat: Go back to your rulers and say to them: cut off the hand of the thief. For he who does not cut off the hand of the thief has in his intention to steal, which is why he fears for his hand; when you mention the matter of cutting off the thief's hand to him, his hand trembles. Those who oppose the limits of Allah themselves proceed on the principle that the destruction of a third is permissible to reform two-thirds, yet the limits of Allah stick in their throats like a bone.

The hundred lashes apply to the unmarried (ghayr muhsan) adulterer, meaning one not married. As for the married one, he has another ruling not found in the Book of Allah, but found in the Sunnah of the Messenger of Allah (ﷺ). This is because the Noble Qur'an is not a book of method only; it is a book of method, miracle, and accompanying principles. Among these principles is that in one of its verses it said that We entrusted the Messenger of Allah with legislating for people.

A ruling derived from speech is open to our quibbling and to our standing before it, turning its words over or interpreting them; but if the ruling is taken from the act of the Legislator, there is no doubt or quibbling in it, and it is not open to interpretation, because it is an act. The Messenger did act, and stoned the married adulterer and adulteress in the story of Ma'iz and al-Ghamidiyya, for he was entrusted by Allah.

We must distinguish between the two punishments. As for the punishment of a slave-woman if she commits adultery, the Exalted says: ﴿Upon them is half the punishment of free married women...﴾ (4:25). Some understood from the verse that it includes both stoning and flogging, and said: for flogging one may give her fifty lashes, but how can stoning be divided? And since stoning cannot be divided, she is not to be stoned.

Had these people reflected on the text of the verse, they would have come out of this disagreement. The Almighty did not say ﴿Upon them is half the punishment of free married women...﴾ and stop; rather He said ﴿...of the punishment﴾ (4:25), thereby specifying the punishment of flogging, because punishment (adhab) is painful affliction, whereas stoning is the taking of life. The two are contrasted.

Do you not see the Qur'an's words in the story of Solomon, peace be upon him, and the hoopoe: ﴿I will surely punish him with a severe punishment or slaughter him...﴾ (27:21). Punishment is other than slaughter.

So the division of the punishment applies to flogging only; as for stoning, it is not divided. If a married slave-woman commits adultery, she is stoned.

As for His saying: ﴿if you should believe in Allah and the Last Day...﴾ (24:2): this is painful speech and a stirring of the community of believers. This is the ruling, and this is the punishment Allah has legislated. If you believe in Allah and in reckoning and punishment, then apply the law of Allah; otherwise, re-examine your faith in Allah and the Last Day, for we doubt the truthfulness of this faith.

It is as if the Blessed and Exalted were stirring us up and rousing us against the people of this crime, so that we might seize their hands and frighten them with the limits Allah has legislated.

The meaning is: if you believe in Allah as a wise God, Legislator, who created creation and wills to protect His creatures and purify them so that they may be fit for His true vicegerency on earth, then leave the Creator to dispose of His dominion and His creatures according to His will, Mighty is He. The creation is not your creation for you to interfere in it.

Then He, Exalted, says: ﴿And let a group of the believers witness their punishment.﴾ (24:2): the matter does not stop at torment and flogging; a group of believers must witness this punishment. The "ta'ifa" is a group, and its minimum is four. Why? They say: because the soul may bear humiliation if it is a secret that no one sees; it is not painful to him that you torment him with the severest torment between you and him, but he cannot bear that you insult him in front of people. Therefore witnessing the punishment is a humiliation to its recipient, and also a deterrent to the spectator and a practical, restraining example.

Thus they say: the limits are deterrents and expiations. Deterrents for whoever witnesses them, i.e., they restrain him from committing what calls for this limit; and expiations for the one upon whom the limit is applied, they atone for his sin and remove from him the punishment of the Hereafter. It is not possible that one who confessed and had the limit applied to him be equal to one who did not confess. And since adultery was never established by witnesses, it was established only by confession.

(1) From Aisha (may Allah be pleased with her), who said: A man came to the Messenger of Allah (ﷺ) and said: "I am ruined." The Messenger of Allah (ﷺ) said: "Why?" He said: "I had intercourse with my wife in Ramadan during the day." He said: "Give charity, give charity." He said: "I have nothing." So he told him to sit, and then there came to him two baskets containing food. The Messenger of Allah (ﷺ) commanded him to give it in charity. Recorded by Muslim in his Sahih (1112).

(2) From Abu Bakr (may Allah be pleased with him) that the Messenger of Allah (ﷺ) said: "Whoever is given authority over any matter of the Muslims and appoints someone over them out of favoritism, upon him is the curse of Allah; Allah will not accept from him any exchange or ransom until He admits him into Hell." Recorded by Ahmad in his Musnad (1/6).

Al-Sha'rawi says: The Truth, glory be to Him, says: {{The fornicator shall not marry except a fornicatress or an idolatress, and the fornicatress none shall marry except a fornicator or an idolater, and that has been forbidden to the believers (3)}}

﴿The fornicator shall not marry except a fornicatress or an idolatress…(3)﴾ [an-Nur]: Because marriage is founded on equality (takafu') so that neither spouse looks down upon the other. The fornicator has baseness in him, so only a base person like himself suits him, namely a fornicatress, or a baser one, who is the idolatress, because shirk (association of partners with Allah) is baser than zina (fornication), since zina is the violation of a directive command from Allah, whereas shirk is disbelief in Allah. Therefore the idolatress is more corrupt than the fornicatress. What we say about the marriage of the male fornicator we say about the marriage of the female fornicatress: ﴿And the fornicatress none shall marry except a fornicator or an idolater…(3)﴾ [an-Nur]. Here some object: how is it, if the fornicatress is a Muslim, that an idolater would marry her? They said: the contrast here is intended only for censure and denunciation, not for permission, because a Muslim woman may never marry an idolater at all; so the verse is a rebuke to her: "O base one, none suits you but a base person like yourself, or a baser one."

And I see that the text admits of a separation of the aspect, because the woman who committed zina revolves between two matters: either she embraced zina while knowing that it is forbidden, in which case she is a sinner who remains Muslim, or she rejected the ruling on zina and objected to it, in which case she is an idolatress. In this latter case our understanding of the verse holds together.

Then He, exalted is He, says: ﴿And that has been forbidden to the believers (3)﴾ [an-Nur]: This is the reason for the purity of lineages: that Allah the Exalted forbids zina, so that the offspring comes forth pure in lineage and origin, cherished by a father and a mother, enveloped in the warmth of the family, none bearing upon him even a breath of the air, because he came from a good, pure and clean vessel.

- Ahmad in his Musnad (2/159, 222) related from Abdullah ibn Umar that a man from among the believers asked the Messenger of Allah (ﷺ) for permission regarding a woman called Umm Mahzul, who used to commit fornication and stipulated with him that she would spend on him. So he asked the Messenger of Allah (ﷺ), or mentioned her affair to him, and the Messenger of Allah (ﷺ) recited this verse to him. Al-Wahidi also related it in Asbab al-Nuzul (p. 180).
- At-Tirmidhi in his Sunan (3177) and Abu Dawud in his Sunan (2051) related from Abdullah ibn Amr ibn al-As, who said: There was a man called Marthad ibn Abi Marthad, a man who used to carry captives from Makkah until he brought them to Madinah, and there was a prostitute in Makkah called Anaq, who was a friend of his. He said to the Messenger of Allah (ﷺ): "Shall I marry Anaq? Shall I marry Anaq?" The Messenger of Allah (ﷺ) held back and did not answer him until this verse was revealed, and the Messenger of Allah (ﷺ) said: "O Marthad, the fornicator shall not marry except a fornicatress or an idolatress, so do not marry her."

Commentary of al-Sha'rawi (Tafsir al-Sha'rawi, surahs 1-53, fragments of 54-66) on surah 24, verse 4:

Then the Truthful, glorified is He, says:

﴿And those who accuse chaste women and then do not bring four witnesses, lash them eighty lashes, and never accept their testimony, and those are the defiantly disobedient.﴾

Al-ramy (the throwing): hurling one thing at another. Al-muhsanat: the plural of muhsana, from al-ihsan, which is protection. From it we say, for example, "So-and-so has parliamentary immunity (hasanah barlamaniyyah)." That means the law has undertaken to protect him, so if they wish to hold him to account or prosecute him, they first lift the immunity from him. From the same root is also the word al-hisn (fortress), which is the impregnable thing that protects whoever is within it.

He, exalted is He, says: ﴿And We taught him the craft of making armour for you, to protect you from your violence..﴾ [al-Anbiya' 80]: meaning the coats of mail that protect a person and keep him safe in war.

Al-muhsanat is applied to married women, because she has protected herself through marriage from inclining toward immorality. It is also applied to free women, because in the past it was the slave women who were put forward for prostitution, while free women never submitted to it.

Thus, Hind (1), whom we now honour after her conversion to Islam, and who chewed the liver of our master Hamza in the Battle of Uhud, but there is no blame on her now, for Islam wipes out what came before it. When Hind heard the Messenger of Allah (ﷺ) forbidding women from fornication, she said: "Would a free woman commit fornication?", because fornication had spread before Islam among the prostitutes from among the slave women, to the extent that they had banners that they raised over their houses so that they would be recognised by them.

The meaning: those who accuse chaste women of what contradicts chastity, meaning fornication. ﴿Then do not bring four witnesses, lash them eighty lashes..﴾ [al-Nur 4]: this is called the punishment for slander (hadd al-qadhf), that you accuse a free woman of fornication and charge her with it. In this case you must bring four witnesses who testify to what you accused her of. If you do not do so, the punishment for slander is enforced upon you, eighty lashes. Then the matter does not end at the lashing; rather, your testimony is never accepted after that.

﴿And never accept their testimony..﴾ [al-Nur 4]: Why? Because he is no longer fit for it, for he is a corrupt person (fasiq). ﴿And those are the defiantly disobedient﴾ [al-Nur 4]: and the corrupt person has no testimony. Thus the Wise Lawgiver combined for the slanderer the punishment of lashing, then removed his standing from society by the loss of his testimony, then described him after that as corrupt. So in his society he has fallen from esteem and fallen from honour.

All of this is to deter everyone whose soul tempts him to plunge into the honour of free women and accuse pure women. That is why slander is expressed by "ramy" (throwing), because it is often done in haste and without evidence. Allah, blessed and exalted, wants to protect the community of faith from having immorality spread within it, or even the mere mention of it and talk of it.

1. She is Hind bint 'Utba ibn Rabi'a, mother of Mu'awiya ibn Abi Sufyan. She was the wife of Abu Sufyan ibn Harb, and she is the one who chewed the liver of Hamza, paternal uncle of the Messenger of Allah (ﷺ), in the Battle of Uhud after Wahshi killed him at her instigation.

2. Cited by Ibn Kathir in his tafsir (4/353), in the commentary on the verse ﴿O Prophet, when believing women come to you pledging allegiance to you that they will not associate anything with Allah, nor steal, nor commit fornication..﴾ [al-Mumtahana 12]. In it she said: "O Messenger of Allah, does a free woman commit fornication?" He said: "No, by Allah, a free woman does not commit fornication."

Commentary of al-Sha'rawi (Tafsir al-Sha'rawi, surahs 1-53, fragments of 54-66) on surah 24, verse 5:

Then the Truth, glory be to Him, says:

﴿Except for those who repent after that and make amends. Indeed, Allah is Forgiving and Merciful.﴾ (5)

The scholars differed over the meaning of the exception here: is it an exception from "wickedness" (fisq), or an exception from the non-acceptance of their testimony?

We have mentioned that the legislation of repentance (tawbah) is a favour and a generosity from the Truth, blessed and exalted is He, for if repentance were not legislated, whoever fell into sin once and whose repentance was not accepted would become bold in disobedience and would multiply it. And why would he not? He would have no deterrent to give it up.

So, when Allah legislates repentance, He is in fact protecting society from those who have lost hope, who have sold their souls and despaired of salvation. Thus the legislation of repentance is a generosity, and its acceptance is another generosity. For this reason the Truth, glory be to Him, says: ﴿Then He turned to them in forgiveness so that they might repent...﴾ (118) [al-Tawbah]: that is, He legislated repentance for them so that they would repent and it would be accepted from them.

His saying, exalted is He: ﴿And make amends...﴾ (5) [al-Nur] indicates that whoever has committed an evil deed must follow it with a good one. A noble hadith has been transmitted: "Follow the evil deed with a good deed and it will erase it..." (1) Therefore you find that those who have been excessive towards themselves in some respect, when they grow old and love repentance, are seen to be eager for the love of goodness and the performance of acts of obedience, wishing thereby to expiate the evil deeds that preceded them. This is in contrast to one who has guarded himself and kept himself far from sins, for you find him indifferent in that regard, doing good according to his capacity.

It is as though the Truth, blessed and exalted is He, is warning His servants: O My servants, beware. Whoever takes from Me something stealthily, or abandons My judgment, or dares to disobey Me, will become weary afterwards and will meet with the bitterest of troubles, because the evil deed will remain behind him, pursuing him and wearing him down until I forgive it for him, and he will need many good deeds and acts of goodness to make up for his shortcoming in the right of his Lord.

(1) Related by Ahmad in his Musnad (5/153, 158), al-Tirmidhi in his Sunan (1987), and al-Darimi in his Sunan (2/323), from the hadith of Abu Dharr (may Allah be pleased with him), who said: the Messenger of Allah (ﷺ) said: "Fear Allah wherever you are, follow the evil deed with a good deed and it will erase it, and deal with people with good character." The wording is that of al-Tirmidhi.

Commentary of al-Sha'rawi (Tafsir al-Sha'rawi, surahs 1-53, fragments of 54-66) on surah 24, verse 6:

Then the Exalted One says:

﴿And those who accuse their wives, and have no witnesses except themselves, then the testimony of one of them is four testimonies by Allah, that he is surely of the truthful. (6) And the fifth [testimony] is that the curse of Allah be upon him if he is of the liars. (7)﴾

After the Exalted and Blessed One spoke about those who accuse chaste women and explained the ruling on slander (qadhf), He wished to explain the ruling on accusation when it comes from a husband against his wife, because the matter here is different. There may be children between them, from him or from another, so he must be disciplined by the discipline of the Shari'ah and not wound the children by accusing their mother when they have no fault.

Therefore Allah, glory be to Him, prescribed in this case a specific ruling for it, which is the mula'anah (mutual cursing), and this verse has been called the verse of li'an (the oath of cursing).

It is narrated that Hilal ibn Umayyah went to the Messenger of Allah (ﷺ) and said: "O Messenger of Allah, I saw a man on the belly of my wife. If I leave him, I would have to bring four witnesses, and by then he would have satisfied his need and left. And if I kill him, I would have transgressed against him."(2)

So, what is the solution to this riddle?

We should know that Allah, the Exalted, does not send down legislation and judgment at the outset; rather, He leaves in the universe, from the affairs and events of life, what requires this judgment, so that the judgment descends and meets the need for it, as they say: "the place of water for one who is thirsty and parched." That is: when the judgment descends it has a place, and people receive it, feeling that it was sent down for their sake, after they had been longing for a ruling on a matter on which no ruling had come.

Allah prescribed the ruling of mula'anah, or li'an specifically, for this case in which a husband observes something concerning his family, and may even lay his hand on it, but cannot bring witnesses to establish this situation. Therefore the Wise Lawgiver made him stand alone in this testimony, repeating it four times in place of the four witnesses.

He says: "I call Allah to witness that I am truthful in what I have accused my wife of," saying it four times. In the fifth he says: "The curse of Allah be upon me if I am a liar." Thus the husband's role in the mula'anah ends.

(1) Occasion of revelation: It is narrated from Ibn 'Abbas that he said: When the verse "And those who accuse chaste women, then do not bring four witnesses, lash them eighty lashes..." (4) [al-Nur] was revealed, Sa'd ibn 'Ubadah, who was the chief of the Ansar, said: "Is it revealed in this way, O Messenger of Allah?" The Prophet (ﷺ) said: "Do you not hear, O assembly of the Ansar, what your chief says?" They said: "O Messenger of Allah, he is a jealous man. By Allah, he has never married a woman except a virgin, and he has never divorced a woman, so that any man among us would dare to marry her, out of the intensity of his jealousy." Sa'd said: "By Allah, O Messenger of Allah, I know that it is true and that it is from Allah, but I wonder: if I were to find a fornicator (laka') with his thigh upon a woman, I would not be permitted to disturb him or move him until I bring four witnesses. By Allah, I would not bring them until he had satisfied his need." Not long after, Hilal ibn Umayyah came from his land in the evening and found a man with his wife. He saw with his eyes and heard with his ears, and did not disturb him until morning. Then he went in the morning to the Messenger of Allah (ﷺ) and informed him of what had happened. The Messenger of Allah disliked what he had brought and was distressed by it. Sa'd ibn 'Ubadah said: "Now the Messenger of Allah (ﷺ) will strike Hilal ibn Umayyah and nullify his testimony among the Muslims." Hilal said: "By Allah, I hope that Allah will make a way out for me from it." Then the verse "And those who accuse their wives, and have no witnesses except themselves..." (6) [al-Nur] was revealed. The Messenger of Allah (ﷺ) said: "Rejoice, O Hilal, for Allah has made for you relief and a way out." He said: "I had hoped for that from my Lord." And he mentioned the rest of the hadith. Narrated by al-Wahidi in Asbab al-Nuzul (pp. 180, 181).

(2) The wording of the hadith in the Musnad of Imam Ahmad (1/238), from the hadith of Ibn 'Abbas, may Allah be pleased with them both, that Hilal ibn Umayyah, who was one of the three who were forgiven, came from his land at night and found a man with his family. He saw with his eyes and heard with his ears, and did not disturb him until morning, then went in the morning to the Messenger of Allah (ﷺ) and said: "O Messenger of Allah, I came to my family at night and found a man with her. I saw with my eyes and heard with my ears." The hadith...

After Allah, blessed and exalted is He, spoke of those who accuse chaste women, and explained the ruling on slander (qadhf), He wished to explain the ruling on accusation when it comes from a husband against his wife. The matter here is different, since there may be children between them, born to him or to another, so he must conduct himself with the discipline of the Sharia and must not wound the children by accusing their mother, when they bear no blame.

Therefore, the Truthful Lawgiver, glorified and exalted is He, prescribed for this case a specific ruling, namely mula'ana (li'an, mutual imprecation), and this verse has been named the verse of li'an.

It is narrated that Hilal ibn Umayya went to the Messenger of Allah, peace and blessings be upon him, and said: "O Messenger of Allah, I saw a certain man upon the belly of my wife. If I leave him, I will go and bring four witnesses, by which time he will have satisfied his need and departed; and if I kill him, I will have transgressed against him."

So then: what resolved this riddle?

We should know that Allah, exalted is He, does not send down legislation and rulings at the outset. Rather, He leaves in the universe, among the matters and events of life, what requires this ruling, so that the ruling descends and coincides with the need for it. As they say: "the place of water for one who is parched with thirst" (mawqi' al-ma' min dhi al-ghullah al-sadi). That is, when the ruling descends, it has a place, and people receive it eagerly, feeling that it was sent down for their sake, after they had been looking forward to a ruling on a matter for which no ruling had yet come.

Allah, exalted is He, prescribed the ruling of mula'ana, or li'an, specifically for this case, in which a husband observes something concerning his family, and may even lay his hand upon it, but cannot bring witnesses to prove this situation. Therefore the Wise Lawgiver made him stand alone in this testimony, and repeat it four times in place of the four witnesses.

He says: "I bear witness before Allah that I am truthful in what I have accused my wife of," saying this four times. In the fifth, he says: "May the curse of Allah be upon me if I am a liar." Thus ends the husband's role in the li'an.

(Yadra'u) meaning: it averts, turns away, from the wife the punishment, that she bear witness herself four testimonies by Allah: she says, "I call Allah to witness that he is lying in what he has accused me of." And in the fifth she says: "May the wrath of Allah be upon me if he is among the truthful." If the wife refuses this testimony, then adultery is established against her; if she swears, then they are equal, and neither of them is any longer fit for the other, and at that point the Sharia separates them with a final separation after which there is no return, and he may never remarry her.(1)

1 The narration has come that the wife of Hilal ibn Umayya, whom he accused of adultery with Shurayk ibn Sahma', testified four times that she had not done it. When it came to the fifth testimony she fell silent for a while, until they thought she would confess. Then she said: "I will not disgrace my people for the rest of the day," and she went on with the oath. The Messenger of Allah (ﷺ) then separated them and said: "Look: if she gives birth to him curly-haired, thick-calved, then he belongs to Shurayk ibn Sahma', and if she gives birth to him white, straight-haired, short-eyed, then he belongs to Hilal ibn Umayya." She gave birth to him curly-haired and thick-calved. That is: the woman's lie was confirmed and established, and Hilal's truthfulness was established. Then he (ﷺ) said: "Were it not for what was revealed concerning them in the Book of Allah, there would have been a matter between me and her." Mentioned by Ibn Kathir in his tafsir (3/268).

(Yadra'u) means: the punishment is averted from the wife, so that she too testifies four times by Allah. She says: "I testify by Allah that he is lying regarding what he has accused me of," and in the fifth she says: "May the wrath of Allah be upon me if he is among the truthful."

If the wife refrains from this testimony, then adultery is established against her. If she swears, then the two are equal, and neither of them is fit for the other any longer. At that point the Sharia separates them with a final separation (tafriq) after which there is no return, and he may never marry her again.

This legislation is a favour (fadl) from Allah, because He concluded this matter in the best way it could be concluded. Therefore, after it, He, glorified is He, says:

﴿And were it not for the favour of Allah upon you and His mercy...﴾

This legislation is a favour from God, for He has concluded this matter in the best way it could be concluded. Therefore, after it, He says:

﴿And were it not for the bounty of Allah upon you and His mercy, and that Allah is Accepting of repentance and Wise.﴾

That is: were it not for this, you would have been disgraced, and enmity would have intensified among you. But the bounty of Allah protected you through this wise legislation, which is suited to this situation.

Slander (qadhf) is a heinous crime against the whole of society; through it indecency spreads and ties of kinship are severed. This is so when it is directed at chaste women in general, but it is graver when it is directed at a wife. What then if such a statement is made about a woman who is not the mother of one person alone, but is the mother of all the believers: Umm al-Mu'minin, the Lady 'A'isha, may Allah be pleased with her and make her pleased. It was therefore fitting that the context mention what befell the Lady 'A'isha, which is called the incident of the slander (ifk). Why?

Because Allah, exalted is He, wishes to give us an example in prophethood itself, and wishes to console 'A'isha, the woman of noble lineage and Mother of the Believers, of whom such things were said. Therefore 'A'isha will forever remain an example for every noble woman who is accused in her honour and whose enemies try to disfigure her image. We say to her: "Do not worry, for they said the like of this about 'A'isha."

The verses of the slander (ifk) also stand as proof of the truthfulness of the Messenger of Allah (ﷺ) in conveying the message from his Lord. For they mention that people accuse chaste women, and accuse their own wives, and the most monstrous of all is that they should accuse the wife of the Prophet and Mother of the Believers.

¹ The phrase ﴿And were it not for the bounty of Allah upon you and His mercy...(10)﴾ [al-Nur] is repeated four times in this surah. Abu Yahya Zakariyya al-Ansari said in (Fath al-Rahman bi-kashf ma yaltabis fi al-Qur'an), p. 285: "He repeated it because the answers to it differ. The first answer is elided, its estimated form being: 'it would have disgraced you.' The answer to the second is His words ﴿Surely there would have touched you for what you plunged into a painful punishment (14)﴾ [al-Nur]. The answer to the third is elided, its estimated form being: 'He would have hastened the punishment for you.' The answer to the fourth is His words ﴿None of you would have ever been purified, from anyone, ever (21)﴾ [al-Nur]."

Then He, glorified is He, says:

﴿Indeed, those who came with the slander are a group among you. Do not think it bad for you; rather, it is good for you. For every person among them is what he earned of the sin, and he who took upon himself the greater part of it, for him is a great punishment.﴾ (24:11):

Al-Ifk (slander): We have three kinds of relation (nisba) in events: a mental relation (nisba dhihniyya), a verbal relation (nisba kalamiyya) when you speak, and an external relation (nisba kharijiyya). When I say: "Muhammad is diligent" (mujtahid), this is a mental proposition. If I utter it, it is a verbal relation. Is there a person named Muhammad who is diligent? This is an external relation. If the verbal relation agrees with the external relation, the speech is true; if it disagrees, the speech is false.

Truth is that the verbal relation corresponds to reality, and falsehood is that the verbal relation does not correspond to reality. Falsehood may be unintentional or intentional. If it is intentional, it is al-ifk. If it is unintentional, as when someone informs you that Muhammad is diligent while he is not, then the report is false, but the reporter is not a liar.

Al-ifk, then, is the deliberate telling of a lie, and it is given the opposite of its ruling. For example, you say: "Muhammad is diligent," while you know that he is negligent. For this reason al-ifk is the most atrocious kind of lying, because it inverts facts and fabricates a reality contrary to what has happened.

He, exalted is He, says: ﴿And the overturned cities He hurled down﴾ (53:53) [al-Najm]: these are the towns whose upper parts God made their lower parts. Likewise, al-ifk alters reality and overturns it completely.

Al-'usba (the group): the group whose movement is bound together to achieve a single united goal. From this we say: "a drug gang," "a theft gang," meaning: a group that agreed to carry out an act for one aim. And from it is His saying in Surat Yusuf: ﴿Though we are a group (usba)...﴾ (12:14) [Yusuf].

Since the people of al-ifk were a group, they must have had one goal in defaming and disgracing. Their leader was Abdullah ibn Ubayy ibn Salul, the chief of the hypocrites (munafiqun), and he is excused for being so. On the day the Messenger of God (ﷺ) entered Madina, they were preparing a crown for Abdullah ibn Ubayy to crown him king over Madina. When he was surprised by the Messenger of God and by people gathering around him and deserting him, this remained in his soul.

Therefore he is the one who said: ﴿If we return to Madina, the mightier will surely expel the weaker from it...﴾ (63:8) [al-Munafiqun]: he meant that he himself was the mightier. The Truth, blessed and exalted, replied: "You have spoken truly, but might belongs to God, to His Messenger, and to the believers, and so the one who will be expelled from it is you."

He is also the one who said: ﴿Do not spend on those who are with the Messenger of God until they disperse...﴾ (63:7) [al-Munafiqun]. What is remarkable is that he acknowledges that Muhammad is the Messenger of God and says it openly, yet he denies it by his deeds and conduct, and distorts the thought and the expression.

Since the Exalted One named this incident concerning the Mother of the Believers, 'A'isha, "al-ifk," they must have inverted the facts and said what contradicts reality.

The story happened during the expedition of Banu al-Mustaliq. Whenever he (ﷺ) wished to undertake an expedition, he would draw lots among his wives, to see which of them would go out with him. This is what his justice (ﷺ) required. On this expedition he drew lots, and the lot fell to 'A'isha, so she went out with him. After the expedition, while they were preparing to return, Sayyida 'A'isha said: "I went to relieve myself in the open, then I returned to my howdah, seeking a necklace of mine made of (jizi' Zafar), which is a precious kind."

When Sayyida 'A'isha came back, she found the people had gone, and she did not find her howdah. She said to herself: "They will surely miss me and they will return." But how did the people carry 'A'isha's howdah while she was not in it? They said: because women were light and did not weigh much, and 'A'isha was slender, so men carried her howdah without noticing that she was not inside it. Then Sayyida 'A'isha lay down in the place of her howdah, waiting for someone to come to her. It was the custom of the people that one of them would lag behind after the departure to inspect the place and search it, in case he found something the people had forgotten or a person who had fallen behind the caravan.

This searcher was Safwan ibn al-Mu'attal. When he saw the shape of a sleeping person and approached, behold, it was 'A'isha, may God be pleased with her. He made his camel kneel beside her, and turned his face away until she mounted, and he led her on without looking at her, and kept himself chaste. The evidence is that the Qur'an called what they said "ifk," meaning: contrary to reality. Safwan did nothing but the opposite of what they said.

When Safwan arrived leading his camel with 'A'isha, some of the hypocrites saw him and accused her, and they said about the two of them what is not fitting for the Mother of the Believers. The leader of hypocrisy in Madina, Abdullah ibn Ubayy, and Mistah ibn Uthatha, and Hassan ibn Thabit, and Hamna bint Jahsh, wife of Talha ibn Ubayd Allah and sister of Zaynab bint Jahsh, led this campaign; they spread this accusation and broadcast it among the people.

Then He, glorified is He, says: ﴿Do not think it bad for you; rather, it is good for you...﴾ (24:11) [al-Nur]. But what good is there in this speech and in its spreading? They said: because the Qur'an, when 'A'isha is accused and her innocence is sent down from above the seven heavens in a Qur'an that is recited and worshipped by until the Day of Resurrection, and when a people are disgraced on the tongue of the Qur'an, others must take heed, and fear that if they commit a similar violation their affair will be exposed. Therefore this situation became a practical lesson for the community of faith.

Yes, this incident became good, because it was a kind of support for the Messenger of God and for his call. The Truth, blessed and exalted, supports His Messenger in matters that gladden, to cut off the hope of his enemies of triumphing over him, even by deception, by cunning, and by secret plotting. At the height of Quraysh's enmity toward the Messenger of God, people's faith in him kept increasing day after day.

They conspired against him and plotted against him by night on the night of the Hijra, but they did not succeed. Then they tried to bewitch him, and indeed they made a sorcery for him, and placed it in the well of Dhharwan, in a comb and combings. Gabriel, peace be upon him, informed him of this, so the Messenger of God (ﷺ) sent 'Ali, who went and brought it.

So: they were defeated in open confrontation, they were defeated in plotting and scheming, and they were defeated even in using the jinn and seeking their help. Here too they were defeated in distorting the image of prophethood and attacking its reputation. As if the Truth, glorified is He, were saying to His enemies: cut off your hope, for you will never reach Muhammad. From here the incident of al-ifk became good for the community of believers.

Nevertheless, no one dared to inform Sayyida 'A'isha of what the hypocrites were saying about her, but the Messenger of God (ﷺ) changed toward her: he no longer joked with her as was his custom, and he would enter upon her and say: "How are you?" 'A'isha noticed this change but did not know its cause, until it happened that she walked with Umm Mistah, one of these hypocrites, and she stumbled and said: "Mistah is ruined." 'A'isha rebuked her: "How do you curse your son?" She said: "Do you not know what he says?" Then Sayyida 'A'isha went to her mother and asked her about what the people were saying, and her mother informed her.

Therefore, when the innocence of 'A'isha was revealed in the Qur'an, Abu Bakr said to her: "Stand up and thank the Messenger of God." She said: "Rather, I thank God, who cleared me."

Then the Truth, glorified is He, says: ﴿For every person among them is what he earned of the sin...﴾ (24:11) [al-Nur]:

The verb kasaba (simple form) is usually used for good, and the verb iktasaba (form VIII, indicating effort and deliberateness) for evil. Why? They said: because doing good accords with the nature of the soul, and harmonizes with its constitution and makeup; so one who undertakes a good deed does not resist anything in himself, nor oppose a faculty of his faculties or a habit of his habits.

We observe this even in animals. Do you not see the cat: if you put a piece of meat before it, it sits beside you and eats it; but if you snatch it from you suddenly, it flees with it and eats it far from you. So in the human self and constitution, and even in animals, there is something by which good and evil, right and wrong, are recognized.

If you look at your daughter or your wife, you are natural and at ease, because the faculties of your soul are in harmony with you and do not oppose you in this act. But if you try to look at what is not lawful for you, you steal the glance and snatch it, and try to conceal it so that no one notices, and you may become flustered and your color may change. Why? Because you are doing something unnatural, to which you have no right, so the faculties of your soul and the particles of your constitution oppose you. The natural matter is responded to by the soul spontaneously, whereas wrong and evil need effort. Therefore He expressed plotting, scheming and cunning with iktasaba, which indicates effort.

And the saying of the Blessed and Exalted: ﴿And he who took upon himself the greater part of it, for him is a great punishment (24:11)﴾ [al-Nur]:

Tawalla kibr al-shay' means: he undertook it and had a full share in it; or we say: he was deeply involved in it. The intended one here is Abdullah ibn Ubayy, who led this campaign and undertook to carry it out and spread it. ﴿For him is a great punishment (24:11)﴾ [al-Nur]: that is, one fitting to this crime.
