Commentary of al-Sha'rawi (Tafsir al-Sha'rawi, surahs 1-53, fragments of 54-66) on surah 24, verse 12:

﴿Why, when you heard it, did the believing men and believing women not think well of their own kind and say, "This is a manifest lie"?﴾ (24:12):

Allah, blessed and exalted, directs us to what ought to be the case in such a trial: the believers should have confidence in themselves and in their faith, should think well of one another, and should keep themselves far from accusations of this kind, which do not befit the community of believers. So it was incumbent that the first ear to hear these words, and the first tongue to utter them, should reject them. For Allah, exalted be He, would not deceive His Messenger and the elite of His creation by making his wife an object of doubt and accusation, let alone attributing to her this monstrous crime.

﴿Why, when you heard it, did the believing men and believing women not think well of their own kind and say, "This is a manifest lie"?﴾ [An-Nur]: Before the Qur'an descended with her innocence, it was expected that immunity would come from the believers' own souls, so that they would reject this talk.

"Lawla" (لولا, "why not" or "if only") is a particle of urging and exhortation. He said "the believing men and the believing women" (al-mu'minun wal-mu'minat) because men and women both took part in this trial, and the Qur'an does not urge them to think well of the Messenger of Allah or of his wife, but to think well of their own kind, because such a matter does not befit believers. How much less does it befit the wife of the Prophet of Allah and His Messenger (ﷺ)?

﴿And say...﴾ [An-Nur]: that is, before the Qur'an descended to declare her innocent, ﴿"This is a manifest lie."﴾ [An-Nur]: meaning a deliberate, clear and evident falsehood, since it concerns whom? It concerns the Mother of the Believers, whom Allah purified and chose as the wife of His Messenger (ﷺ).

Then the Truthful One, glorified is He, says:

﴿Why did they not bring four witnesses for it? So when they do not bring the witnesses, then those, with Allah, are the liars.﴾

It has already been mentioned in the verses the ruling on slander (qadhf), and that whoever accuses a chaste woman (muhsanah) of this charge must bring four witnesses to establish the truth of what he has said. If he does not bring them, then he is a liar in the sight of Allah, and the prescribed punishment for slander (hadd al-qadhf) must be carried out against him.

Then He, exalted is He, says:

﴿And were it not for the grace of Allah upon you and His mercy in this world and the Hereafter, you would have been touched for what you plunged into with a great punishment.﴾ (24:14)

﴿Afadtum (أفضتم)...﴾ (24:14): to rush headlong into a matter with the intention of haste. The meaning of haste is that a great event takes place in a shorter time than one would imagine for it, like a distance you walk in two minutes which you hurry to cover in one minute. It is as though they hastened into this speech when they heard it, just as they say: "He plunged into it and dove in" (khabba fiha wa wada').

But why did Allah show them grace and mercy, so that the punishment did not touch them, and did not requite them for their slander of the Mother of the Believers?

They said: Because the Truth, blessed and exalted is He, intended from this matter a lesson and an admonition, and made it for the believers a means of clarification. So the purpose is not that Allah should send down punishment upon them, but rather that He should teach them and give them a lesson in protecting the honour of the believers.

Commentary of al-Sha'rawi (Tafsir al-Sha'rawi, surahs 1-53, fragments of 54-66) on surah 24, verse 15:

﴿When you received it with your tongues, and uttered with your mouths what you had no knowledge of, and you thought it a trifling matter, while it was, in the sight of Allah, grave.﴾ (24:15)

Consider the eloquence of the Qur'anic expression in describing the speed with which this talk was spread and circulated without awareness and without reflection. It is well known that news is received by the ear, not by the tongue. Yet, because of the speed with which this talk was passed along, it is as though they received it with their tongues: as if the stage of hearing with the ear had been cancelled, so that as soon as they heard it, they spoke.

﴿And you uttered with your mouths what you had no knowledge of (24:15)﴾: "with your mouths" means merely talk passed along from mouth to mouth, without anyone examining it closely. Therefore it says afterwards, ﴿what you had no knowledge of﴾. This talk is not a trifling matter as you think; rather it is grave in the sight of Allah, because it touches the honour of a believer, and a believer has his sanctity. How much more so if that was said about the Messenger of Allah (ﷺ)?

Then the Truthful, Glorified be He, says:

﴿Why, when you heard it, did you not say: "It is not for us to speak of this. Glory be to You! This is a tremendous slander."﴾

This is what you should have responded to this report with: that you should have said, "It is not permissible for us, nor fitting for us, to pass on such talk." The word ﴿Glory be to You﴾ (subhanaka) is said when surprised by the occurrence of something. The meaning is: "Glory be to God; we declare Him far above and exalted beyond permitting such a shameful lie against His Messenger (ﷺ)." This is speech that is not right for us to utter, even in negation, for if affirming such talk is a crime, then speaking in denial of it carries the implication that it may have happened.

It is like when you say: "So-and-so is a man of scrupulous piety," or "the shaykh so-and-so does not drink wine." Despite the negation, you have in effect made it a possibility, so it is not right to attribute evil to him even by way of denial, for that is a dispraise of him, not a praise.

Likewise, speaking of this accusation is not fitting for the Mother of the Believers, even in negation. The meaning of ﴿a tremendous slander﴾ is: a lie that stuns the one who hears it, astonishing him by its enormity and monstrousness. Thus we disdain to utter this talk, even if we are deniers of it.

Commentary of al-Sha'rawi (Tafsir al-Sha'rawi, surahs 1-53, fragments of 54-66) on surah 24, verse 17:

﴿God admonishes you never to return to the like of this, if you are believers. (17) And God makes the signs clear to you, and God is All-Knowing, All-Wise. (18)﴾:

Al-wa'z (admonition): it is that one reaches the summit of things and then admonishes concerning them, as a man who senses his end tries to admonish and advise his children, yet he does not advise them about every matter of life, but only about the important matters that represent the summit of the affairs of life. The admonition of the Truth, blessed and exalted is He, to His servants comes from His gentleness and mercy, exalted is He: "He admonishes you," because it is dear to Him that He should punish you for your sins.

As for the closing of the verse with this condition, ﴿if you are believers (17)﴾ [al-Nur]: it is an incitement and stirring of the community of believers, so that they may desist from such speech and not fall into it again. It is as though He, exalted is He, is saying to them: if you return to the like of this, then review your faith, for your faith at that time will be an incomplete faith, open to doubt.

Repeated text, because it is shared with verse 17: ﴿God exhorts you never to return to the like of it, if you are believers (17). And God makes the signs clear to you, and God is All-Knowing, All-Wise (18)﴾:

Exhortation (wa'z): it is that the summit of things comes and one exhorts by them, like a man who, when he feels his end approaching, tries to exhort his children and advise them, but he does not advise them about all matters of life, rather about the important matters that represent the summit of the affairs of life. And the exhortation of the Truth, blessed and exalted is He, to His servants is from His gentleness and mercy: "He exhorts you," because it is difficult for Him that He should punish you for your sins.

As for the closing of the verse with this condition: ﴿if you are believers (17)﴾ [An-Nur]: it is an urging and stirring of the community of believers, so that they desist from such talk and do not fall into it again; and it is as if He, exalted, is saying to them: if you return to the like of this, then review your faith, for your faith at that time will be incomplete and doubtful.

Then the Almighty says:

﴿Indeed, those who love that indecency (al-fāḥishah) should spread among those who believe will have a painful punishment in this world and the Hereafter. And Allah knows, while you do not know.﴾ (24:19):

﴿Who love…﴾ (24:19): Love is an act of the heart, speech is an act of the tongue, and it is the practical expression of what is in the heart. So the meaning is: those who love this, even if they do not speak of it, because this matter has stages: it begins with love, which is an act of the heart, then talking about it, then listening to it without denouncing it.

Because of the gravity of this crime, Allah the Almighty mentioned its first stage, which is merely an act of the heart that has not turned into inclination, action, or speech. So the matter is serious.

Some people think that spreading indecency disgraces only the accused. Yes, it disgraces the accused, but it may end in his death, and it may end in his innocence. But the calamity is that it becomes a bad example in society.

This is a directive from Allah the Almighty concerning a general matter and a principle that must be observed: when you hear news that offends modesty, touches on people's honor, or violates one of Allah's rulings, beware of spreading it among people, because spreading it creates a behavioral model in the listener for one who wants to do the same. He says to himself: "So-and-so did such-and-such, and so-and-so did such-and-such," and he too becomes emboldened to commit such an act. For this reason Allah the Almighty threatened those who spread indecency, publicize it, and broadcast it among people: ﴿For them is a painful punishment in this world and the Hereafter…﴾ (24:19).

Allah the Blessed and Exalted did not protect anyone from disobedience and bad deeds, but worse than the bad deed is spreading it among people. Spreading may concern a respected man, esteemed in his society, whose word is heeded and who has standing. If you hear about him something unbecoming, what you heard may make you lose interest in this person, and lose interest in his good deeds and positive qualities, so it is as if you have deprived society of this man's good deeds.

This matter concerns the wisdom by which Allah conceals the unseen faults of creation from one another. So: concealing people's hidden matters from one another is a great blessing that enriches and develops goodness in society, and it enables you to deal with others and benefit from them with their shortcomings. The poet truly said:

"Take from my knowledge and do not rely on my deeds; hide the fruit and leave the wood for the fire."

Note 1: al-fāḥishah: the ugly deed. And al-fawāḥish: ugly and reprehensible matters [al-Qāmūs al-Qawīm 2/73].

Then the Truthful, glory be to Him, says:

﴿And were it not for the grace of Allah upon you and His mercy, and that Allah is Kind and Merciful.﴾ (24:20):

Look at how much grace from Allah, exalted is He, He bestowed upon His servants in this incident. At every stage of this matter He, glory be to Him, says: ﴿And were it not for the grace of Allah upon you and His mercy...﴾ (24:20). This is evidence that what happened was a blessing and good for the believers, even though they thought otherwise.

But where is the answer to "law la" (were it not for)? The answer is understood from the context, and its estimate is: "You would have been disgraced and destroyed, and such-and-such would have befallen you." You may estimate it however you wish. Nothing prevented all of this from you except the grace of Allah and His mercy.

In another place, the Truthful, glory be to Him, clarifies the status of this grace: ﴿Say: "In the grace of Allah and His mercy—in that let them rejoice; it is better than what they accumulate."﴾ (10:58). So the Truthful, glory be to Him and exalted is He, has legislated a method and loves the one who acts by it, but the servant's joy is not complete merely by the act; rather it is through the grace of Allah and His mercy in accepting this act. Thus, the grace of Allah is the common factor in every shortcoming of creation in the method of the Creator, mighty and majestic is He.

Commentary of al-Sha'rawi (Tafsir al-Sha'rawi, surahs 1–53, fragments of 54–66) on surah 24, verse 21:

After this incident, Allah the Exalted had to say:

﴿O you who have believed, do not follow the footsteps of Satan. And whoever follows the footsteps of Satan – indeed, he enjoins immorality and wrongdoing. And if not for the bounty of Allah upon you and His mercy, not one of you would have ever been pure, [i.e., never have become pure] ever. But Allah purifies whom He wills, and Allah is Hearing and Knowing.﴾ (24:21)

It is as if Satan has many footsteps, not a single step. Allah has affirmed his enmity towards the children of Adam, and it is an enmity with consequences, not mere theoretical talk. He is an enemy by an established fact: he refused to prostrate to Adam, disobeyed Allah's command to him, and even revealed what was in his soul, saying: ﴿I am better than him; You created me from fire and You created him from clay.﴾ (7:12)

And he said: ﴿Shall I prostrate to one whom You created from clay?﴾ (17:61). Thus he justified his refusal by claiming superiority, and it is as if his enmity toward Adam was the enmity of envy for Adam's rank and standing with his Lord.

When Allah, Blessed and Exalted, informs us of Satan's enmity through his refusal to prostrate, He is in fact warning us against him, alerting us to his danger, and cultivating in us immunity against Satan. This is because his enmity towards us is focused enmity, not an enmity he practises haphazardly; rather, it is an enmity that has a method and a plan.

The first element of this plan is that he knew how to swear an oath, so he entered upon man through the gate of the might of Allah above His creation, saying: ﴿By Your might, I will surely mislead them all.﴾ (38:82)

Had our Lord – Mighty and Majestic – willed us to be believers, Satan would have had no path over us. But He left us to choice, so Satan entered upon us through this gate. Therefore He said after it: ﴿except Your sincere servants among them.﴾ (15:40) Whoever is characterised by this attribute, Satan has no path to him.

So, this matter of enmity is not between the Truth, Glorified is He, and Satan; rather it is between Satan and the children of Adam.

Then His saying: ﴿O you who have believed…﴾ (24:21) is an address: "O you who have believed in God," as if He is saying: be mindful of the nobility of your faith in Him, and keep away from anything that weakens this faith or undermines the believers by any means, and be certain that Satan has many footsteps.

﴿Do not follow the footsteps of Satan…﴾ (24:21): If he whispers to you from one direction and you resist him and find firmness in you on that side, he turns to another side and beautifies things for you from another gate. Thus your enemy keeps at you until he brings you down. He knows that every person has a point of weakness in his makeup, so he keeps conversing with him until he reaches this point.

Satan is the rebellious, disobedient one among the jinn. The jinn stand in contrast to mankind: among them are the obedient and the disobedient, and the disobedient among them is Satan, and at their head is Iblis. Therefore Allah says in Surat al-Kahf: ﴿except Iblis; he was of the jinn and departed from the command of his Lord…﴾ (18:50).

We have previously mentioned that you can distinguish between disobedience that comes from the self (nafs) and disobedience that comes from Satan. The self insists on a specific sin and does not go beyond it to others, whereas Satan wants you to be disobedient in any way whatsoever: if you resist him in one sin, he drags you into another sin, whatever it may be.

Then He, Glorified is He, says: ﴿And whoever follows the footsteps of Satan – indeed, he enjoins immorality and wrongdoing…﴾ (24:21). And you may ask: where is the answer to the conditional "whoever" (man) here? It is said: the answer has been omitted because it is understood from the context, and it is indicated by mentioning its cause and its effecter. You may supply the answer as: whoever follows the footsteps of Satan, his Lord will make him taste the punishment of the Blaze, because Satan only enjoins immorality and wrongdoing; so whoever follows his steps has nothing but punishment. Thus the cause took the place of the answer of the condition.

This speech is not the speech of a human being; it is the speech of the Lord of the worlds. The style of the Qur'an is an elevated style that requires a conscious mind that grasps the meanings, and it is not mere words and filler.

Do you not see the eloquence of concision in His saying in Surat an-Naml: ﴿Take this letter of mine and deliver it to them; then turn away from them and see what they return.﴾ (27:28)

Then He says after it: ﴿She said, "O eminent ones, indeed a noble letter has been delivered to me."﴾ (27:29)

Consider what lies between these two events of omitted occurrences, which are omitted because they are known. The reader's awareness and perceptiveness do not need us to say: "So the hoopoe went… and so on." These are events that the mind orders on its own.

Satan himself has clarified these steps and announced them, and explained his methods of seduction. Did he not say: ﴿I will surely sit in wait for them on Your straight path.﴾ (7:16) So Satan has no need for the people of the crooked path, because they are his followers. Satan does not go to the tavern, for example; rather he goes to the mosque to corrupt the prayer of those who pray. Therefore some people are disturbed by the whisperings that afflict them in their prayer, and in reality this is a healthy sign of faith. Had you not been in obedience and worship, he would not have whispered to you.

But our misfortune is that Satan gives us only the end of the thread, and we then follow him, unravelling it (nakr fi al-khayt karran). If, whenever Satan whispers to us, we sought refuge with Allah from the accursed Satan, as our Lord, Blessed and Exalted, commanded us: ﴿And if an evil suggestion from Satan should tempt you, then seek refuge in Allah.﴾ (7:200)

So: beware of accepting from him the end of the thread, for if you accept it, you will not be able to control him afterwards.

Among the steps of Satan is also His saying: ﴿Then I will surely come to them from before them and from behind them and from their right and from their left…﴾ (7:17)

So, Satan has a fixed method and plan for misleading man: he comes to man from his four directions: from in front of him, from behind him, from his right, and from his left. But nothing is mentioned about above and below, because the first indicates the exaltation of Lordship and the other the lowliness of servanthood, when you raise your hands upward in supplication and when you place your forehead on the ground in prostration. Therefore your enemy does not come at you from these two directions.

Then Allah the Exalted says: ﴿And if not for the bounty of Allah upon you and His mercy, not one of you would have ever been pure…﴾ (24:21)

We have said that the recompense of reward is shared between two matters: recompense by justice, when you take what you deserve, and recompense by bounty, when your Lord gives you beyond what you deserve. Therefore we should say in supplication: "O Allah, deal with us by bounty not by justice, by kindness not by measure, and by compensation not by reckoning. For if our Lord – Mighty and Majestic – dealt with us by justice, we would all be lost."

But in what did this bounty appear? The bounty of Allah upon this nation appeared in that He, Exalted is He, did not punish it with annihilation as He did the previous nations. And the bounty of Allah upon this nation appeared in that He, Exalted is He, gave it immunity before it was exposed to the incident, and warned us long ago of Satan before we fell into sin and before events surprised us. So He, Glorified is He, said: ﴿So We said, "O Adam, indeed this is an enemy to you and your wife…"﴾ (20:117). Otherwise, the human being would have drowned in a whirlpool of sins.

Warning of danger before it occurs cultivates immunity in the self, and our Lord, Mighty and Majestic, did not leave us in heedlessness until we fell into sin, just as we immunise ourselves against diseases so as to acquire the immunity needed to resist them.

As for His saying: ﴿…not one of you would have ever been pure (zakā)…﴾ (24:21): (zakā) means became pure, cleansed and purified. ﴿But Allah purifies whom He wills, and Allah is Hearing and Knowing﴾ (24:21). He said "Hearing and Knowing" because He, Exalted is He, had earlier said: ﴿Indeed, those who love that immorality should be spread among the believers…﴾ (24:19). That was at the conclusion of the incident of the slander, which shook the Islamic society at its summit, and touched the Messenger of Allah (ﷺ), his companion al-Siddiq, his wife Umm al-Mu'minin 'A'isha, and a group of the Companions.

Therefore Allah, Exalted, said: (And Allah is Hearing) of what was said, (Knowing) of what hearts conceal of love for the spreading of immorality.

¹ zakā: became pure and righteous, so he is zakī and she is zakiyya. [al-Qamus al-Qawim 1/287] al-Qurtubi said in his tafsir (6/4742): "That is: he was not guided, nor did he embrace Islam, nor did he recognise right guidance," according to the reading zakā [without tashdid]. As for the reading zakkā [with tashdid]: "That is, His purifying you, cleansing you and guiding you is only by His bounty, not by your deeds."

Then the Truthful One, glory be to Him, says:

﴿And let not those of virtue and wealth among you swear not to give [aid] to their kinsmen, the needy, and the emigrants in the cause of God. Let them pardon and overlook. Do you not wish that God should forgive you? And God is Forgiving and Merciful.﴾ (24:22)

Some of the excellent Companions became entangled in the incident of the slander (ifk), people who had been disposed toward good, but who were seduced by what was said and were drawn along behind those who spread this rumour. Among them was Mistah ibn Uthatha, the son of the maternal aunt of Abu Bakr al-Siddiq, and Abu Bakr used to spend on him and look after him because of his poverty. When he said what he said about Aisha and plunged into speaking against her, Abu Bakr swore that he would not spend on him, although he and his family had been living in Abu Bakr's ample means and bounty, because this trial had caused some people of goodness to hold back from him.

This is a model of one who denies a favour and does not appreciate acts of kindness, and this action makes people averse to good and turns them away from doing good. God, the Exalted, wishes to correct this matter for us. This is a view that does not accord with the nature of faith, for the one who disobeys God regarding you is not repaid except by your obeying God regarding him.

When you leave the one who wronged you to the punishment of God and pardon him yourself, you have left him to the stronger punishment, for if you punish him, you punish him by your own power and capacity, and if you leave his punishment to God, He punishes him according to His own capacity and power, may He be exalted.

Therefore, the one who pardons has a harder heart than the one who takes revenge. We have previously illustrated this by the brother who transgresses against his younger brother: the father comes, finds his little one humiliated and wronged, takes him into his embrace, and tries to satisfy him and compensate him for the injustice his brother inflicted. The situation in this matter is similar, and to God belongs the highest likeness.

From here it is incumbent upon you to be pleased with the one whom God has placed on your side, and to do good to him, not to return the offence with its like.

Therefore, this verse was revealed concerning Mistah ibn Uthatha when Abu Bakr swore that he would not spend on him and on his family, and that he would withhold from him his gift and kindness. It was revealed to correct this outlook for the Siddiq and to direct his attention to the good that remains with God, not with people.

God, the Exalted, says: ﴿And let not those of virtue and wealth among you swear...﴾ (24:22).

﴿Yatali﴾ (يأتل): it is exactly like ﴿i'talā﴾ (اعتلى), and from it comes ﴿ta'allā﴾ (تألى), meaning he swore and made an oath. God, blessed and exalted, addresses the Siddiq Abu Bakr and uses the plural form ﴿ulū﴾ (أولو), which indicates a group, in order to magnify him for the virtue and rank he holds in Islam, for in every respect he has excellence. Therefore He gave him two attributes, just as He gave them to the Prophet (ﷺ): He said to the Siddiq, ﴿and let them pardon and overlook﴾ (24:22), and He said to the Prophet (ﷺ), ﴿so pardon them and overlook﴾ (5:13).

Likewise, do you not see the Siddiq as the second of two in the cave, and the second of two in many matters? He was the second of two in the Hijrah, and the second of two in accepting the first call of Islam. Therefore the Messenger of God (ﷺ) spoke truly when he said of the Siddiq: "I and Abu Bakr were in the Jahiliyyah like two race-horses," meaning in competing in goodness, "I outstripped him to prophethood and he followed me; had he outstripped me to it, I would have followed him."

Since Abu Bakr had many virtues in various respects, God did not address him in the singular form but in the plural, as an honour and magnification.

Do you not see the Siddiq, along with his known forbearance and tenderness of heart, when the Messenger of God (ﷺ) passed to the Highest Companion and the matter of apostasy (riddah) arose, standing and saying: "By God, if they withheld from me a cord (camel's cord) that they used to give to the Messenger of God, I would fight them over it with the sword, even if I found none but myself"?

This was the stance of the Siddiq, tender of heart, gentle in manner, possessed of mercy and compassion, of whom his daughter said: "He was a man who wept much," meaning, he wept abundantly. Yet in the matter of war, Umar opposed him, despite what was known of Umar's severity and harshness toward the disbelievers. But this difference in the stance of each of them proves that Islam is not a nature that dominates the Muslim, rather it is a stance to which the Muslim returns. The stance of apostasy is what made the Siddiq a brave lion, hard of heart; and had Umar been in his place of responsibility and acted as the Siddiq acted, they would have said: "Severity that the people have become accustomed to from Umar."

Thus it is as if Islam does not want to make the Muslim into a particular nature that remains upon him; rather the situation is what shapes you in faith. This is what we mentioned in His saying: ﴿Muhammad is the Messenger of God, and those with him are hard against the disbelievers, merciful among themselves﴾ (48:29).

The Muslim is not created solely for severity, nor solely for mercy; rather he must act in every situation in the manner that suits it, in light of what God has legislated.

So His saying, ﴿those of virtue and wealth among you﴾ (24:22), says to the Siddiq: You are a virtuous, truthful man, and you have ample means, so do not withhold or prefer yourself over others out of constraint. It does not befit one of virtue to sever his tie and kinship over such an error as Mistah committed, especially since he received his punishment as God legislated, being flogged with the prescribed punishment for slander, eighty lashes, and you have no right to punish him after that.

It is part of the tolerance of Islam that whoever has committed a prescribed offence and been punished for it, no one may reproach him for his sin, for he has repented and returned, and God has purified him of it through the prescribed punishment, and the matter is ended. No one may intervene between the servant and his Lord.

It is as if the Truthful One, blessed and exalted, is saying: Return to your virtue, O Abu Bakr, and return to your ampleness, and be connected in manliness, and do not sever your kinship. He, glory be to Him, wishes to purify what is in souls of the traces of this trial that shook the believing community in Medina.

It does not befit one of virtue and wealth to deal with people by strict justice. True, Mistah deserved this severance and this deprivation, but this recompense does not befit the Siddiq, the possessor of virtue and means.

If you were to take a census of the believers in God and of the disbelievers in the universe, you would find that the believers are few and the disbelievers many. Did God say to the soldiers of His goodness in the universe: give to those who believe and withhold from those who disbelieve? It is as if the Truthful One, blessed and exalted, gives us an example in His own Essence, may He be mighty and majestic: just as He gives to those who disbelieve in Him and provides for them, indeed perhaps they are in better condition than those who believe, so you likewise do not withhold your giving from one who has wronged you.

Therefore He, glory be to Him, says in another verse: ﴿And do not make God an obstacle in your oaths to be righteous and fear God and make peace among people. And God is Hearing and Knowing﴾ (2:224).

If you are dutiful toward someone and something has passed from him, do not swear by God that you will not be dutiful to him, for your anger may subside and you want to be dutiful to him, yet you hide behind your oath. So: do not make God an obstacle through an oath that prevents you from good.

Then He, glory be to Him, says: ﴿those who should give to the near of kin and the needy and the emigrants in the cause of God﴾ (24:22). It is true that Mistah is of Abu Bakr's kin and among the needy, but God gives him another distinction: what he said of the description of the emigrant did not remove him from it, and his sin did not remove him from this great honour.

Among God's favours to His servants is that an evil deed does not nullify a good deed; rather, a good deed after an evil one nullifies it, as He, mighty and majestic, said: ﴿Indeed, good deeds remove evil deeds﴾ (11:114).

Despite what Mistah committed, God kept him within the category of the reproached regarding Abu Bakr, and softened the heart toward him, and kept him among the emigrants.

﴿And let them pardon and overlook﴾ (24:22). Pardon (al-'afw) is abandoning punishment for a sin; but you may pardon the sinner and then rebuke him, and reproach him for your pardon, and remind him always that he does not deserve this pardon from you. Therefore our Lord, blessed and exalted, urges us to overlook after pardoning. Overlooking (al-safh) is abandoning reproach and not mentioning the slip to its perpetrator, until the punishment becomes lighter in his sight than your pardon of him.

That is because the Truthful One, when He legislates for mankind what regulates relations among them, takes into account all the faculties of the soul; He does not limit Himself to the lofty faculties alone, but to all the faculties that order creation as a whole, so that each of us takes according to the measure of his faith and his obedience to his Lord's command.

Concerning this He says: ﴿And if you punish, then punish with the like of that with which you were afflicted. But if you are patient, it is better for the patient﴾ (16:126). If we reflect on the reality of equivalence in repelling an offence, we find it difficult to measure: if a person strikes you with one blow, do you have the power to return that blow with exactly the same, in the same manner, with the same force, and the same pain, such that you are not yourself an aggressor? If you reflected on this equivalence, you would prefer pardon instead of entering into other labyrinths.

We previously mentioned the story of the usurer who stipulated with the debtor that if he was late in repayment he would cut a pound of flesh from him. When the man was late in paying, he brought a suit against him before the judge and informed him of the condition between them. The judge was clever and said to the usurer: Take the knife and cut a pound of his flesh, but if you take more we will take it from you, and if you take less we will take it from you. So the usurer backed down, for he could not measure this matter.

If we turn away from retaliation in kind, pardon has room, and the matter ends in the best possible way.

At another level He, glory be to Him, says: ﴿those who restrain anger and pardon people, and God loves the good-doers﴾ (3:134).

Thus the Truthful One, blessed and exalted, gives us levels in repelling an offence: retaliation in kind is one level, restraining anger is one level, pardon is one level, overlooking is one level, and above all of these is the level of doing good to one who has wronged you: ﴿and God loves the good-doers﴾ (3:134).

Then the Truthful One makes Himself an example for His servants, saying: ﴿Do you not wish that God should forgive you?﴾ (24:22). Just as you wish God to forgive your sin, why do you not forgive the one who has wronged you? It is as if our Lord, mighty and majestic, wishes to set right what is between us. Therefore, when this verse was revealed concerning Abu Bakr, he said: Yes, O Lord, I wish it, I wish it, I wish it.

The meaning of ﴿Do you not...﴾ (24:22) is an interrogative particle urging and encouraging this good character. ﴿And God is Forgiving and Merciful﴾ (24:22): whoever takes on the character of God, may He be exalted, let him have forgiveness, and let him have mercy. And which of us does not wish to be characterized by some of God's attributes, to be described as forgiving and merciful?

3 From Abu Sa'id al-Khudri, who said: The Messenger of God (ﷺ) said: "The one who has shown me the most favour in his companionship and his wealth is Abu Bakr. Had I been taking a close friend other than my Lord, I would have taken Abu Bakr. But the brotherhood and affection of Islam [suffice]. No door in the mosque shall remain open except that it be closed, except the door of Abu Bakr." Related by al-Bukhari in his Sahih (3654).
4 A hadith agreed upon. Related by al-Bukhari in his Sahih (7284, 7285), and likewise Muslim in his Sahih (20), Book of Faith, from Abu Hurairah with the wording: "By God, I will fight whoever separates prayer from zakat, for zakat is the right of wealth. By God, if they withheld from me a cord that they used to give to the Messenger of God (ﷺ), I would fight them over withholding it."
5 Related by al-Bukhari in his Sahih (476), Book of Prayer, from Aisha (may God be pleased with her), who said: "Abu Bakr was a man who wept much, not able to control his eyes when he recited the Qur'an."
6 Ibn Kathir mentioned in his tafsir (3/276) that Abu Bakr al-Siddiq (may God be pleased with him) said: "Yes, by God, we wish that You forgive us, O our Lord." Then he returned to Mistah the support he used to give him and said: "I will never withdraw it from him, in return for what he said. By God, I will never benefit him with any benefit ever."

Then the Almighty says:

﴿Indeed, those who accuse chaste, unwary, believing women are cursed in this world and the Hereafter, and theirs will be a great punishment.﴾ (24:23)

We observe that the verses spoke of the legal punishment for slander (hadd al-qadhf) and the incident of the slander (hadith al-ifk). Then came the verse of reproach to Abu Bakr concerning the matter of provision (rizq), and then the context returned to the fundamental matter: the issue of slander. So why did the matter of provision enter into this subject?

They said: Because every conflict involving animosity may have effects related to provision, and provision is guaranteed by God to His servants, since He is the One who brought them into existence, whether believer or unbeliever. When you give to the needy, you are only a intermediary on God's behalf, and God's outstretched hand is by the means of God.

The Blessed and Exalted God respects a person's ownership even though He is the One who provides and gives to him. But once He has given, the gift becomes his property; then, when He urges him to spend, He takes it from him as a loan. Therefore He says: ﴿Who is it that would lend to God a goodly loan?﴾ (2:245). If the affluent spend on the impoverished, God makes it a loan and Himself takes responsibility for its repayment, because God does not retract His gift. Since He has given you provision, He takes it from you only as a loan.

Therefore He says, Exalted is He: ﴿Here you are, being invited to spend in the way of God, but among you are some who are stingy. And whoever is stingy is only being stingy toward himself.﴾ (47:38)

And in another place, concerning wealth, He says: ﴿If He should ask it of you and press you, you would be stingy, and He would bring out your resentments.﴾ (47:37). A person toils in gathering wealth and sweats for it, and it becomes dear to him, so he is stingy with it. Thus God takes it from him as a loan to be returned with an increase. Provision and wealth have this importance because they are the first basis for the cultivation of the vicegerent (khalifah) on earth. Therefore the discussion of the fundamental matter is set aside here, and this verse concerning provision is mentioned.

Among the same pattern is His saying: ﴿Guard over the prayers, and the middle prayer.﴾ (2:238). It was mentioned amid matters related to the waiting period (iddah) and expiation (kaffarah), and the waiting period of a widow. What is the connection between prayer and these matters?

They said: Because disputes that arise often change the human soul and stir its anger. When you stand to perform ablution and prayer, your soul is calmed and reassured, and you receive these matters of disagreement with some acceptance and contentment.

We return to His saying: ﴿Indeed, those who accuse chaste, unwary...﴾ (24:23). The word muhsanat (chaste) has three usages: it means a married woman, because ihsan means protection, as though she protected herself through marriage; or it means virtuous, even if she has not married, as she is chaste in herself; and muhsanah also means free, because prostitution and fornication were specific to slave women.

﴿And the unwary (al-ghafilat)...﴾ (24:23): the plural of ghafilah, who is the one who knows nothing of such matters, and has nothing in mind about this act. Among the evidence for this is what is reported in the noble hadith, that the Messenger of God (ﷺ) asked Barirah, the servant of Lady Aisha: "What do you say about Aisha, O Barirah?" She said: "She kneads the dough, then sleeps beside it, and the poultry come and eat it, and she does not know."(3) This is a metaphor for unwariness, since she was still young and had not matured into adolescence, and with the maturity of adolescence comes the maturity of certainty and faith.

This unwariness is observed in a young girl when you say to her: "Will you marry so-and-so?" She says: "No, I will marry so-and-so," because she does not understand the meaning of the marital relationship. But when she grows up and understands such matters, if marriage is mentioned to her she feels shy and embarrassed to speak of it, because she has come to know what marriage means.

Therefore, when the Sharia commanded that a girl's permission be sought for marriage, her silence was made her consent. If she is silent, this is her permission and evidence of her understanding of this relationship. But if she says: "Yes, I will marry him, because he is handsome and... and...," this means she has not yet understood the meaning of marriage.

So: the unwary person is one who is unaware even of matters of marriage and marital relations, and knows nothing of such things; how could she think of fornication?

Then our Lord, Blessed and Exalted, mentions the punishment for this crime: ﴿They are cursed in this world and the Hereafter, and theirs will be a great punishment.﴾ (24:23)

If the unwary woman is one for whom such matters are not in mind, and who knows nothing even of marriage and the marital relations between man and woman, then how can we say that she is thinking of this crime?

Cursing (al-la'n) is expulsion and removal from God's mercy, and also expulsion and removal from the fold of the believers. The ruling for the slanderer is that the legal punishment be applied to him, then his testimony is dropped and his standing in the society in which he lives is lost. So God combined for him disgrace in this world through the prescribed punishment and loss of standing, along with the punishment of the Hereafter. Thus cursing in this world does not spare him from the punishment of the Hereafter.

We have said that punishment ('adhab) is the infliction of pain upon a living being. Punishment is sometimes described as painful (alim), sometimes as humiliating (muhin), and sometimes as great (azim). These descriptions vary according to the punishment and the one punished. Some people are not pained by the lashing, but are humiliated by it, so for them it is a punishment that humiliates their dignity. As for the great punishment, it exceeds what the imagining mind can conceive, because punishment is the infliction of pain by one who punishes upon one who is punished. In this world, the punished is punished by human hands and according to human capacity, whereas the punishment of the Hereafter is by the might and dominance of God; therefore it is described as great.

2 Ahfa: he pressed him insistently in asking, or demanded it with force and insistence. God says: ﴿If He should ask it of you and press you...(47:37)﴾, meaning: if He strains you by demanding it and insists upon you, you will be stingy. [al-Qamus al-Qawim 1/163]

Ask the slave girl, she will tell you the truth. So the Messenger of God (ﷺ) called Barirah and said: O Barirah, did you see anything in her that made you doubt?" Barirah said: "No, by the One who sent you with truth, the most I have seen in her is that she is a young slave girl who sleeps over the dough, so the poultry come and eat it."
4 The description of punishment as painful (alim) occurs in 72 places in the Qur'an, including: ﴿And for them is a painful punishment because they used to lie﴾ (2:10), and ﴿And for the wrongdoers He has prepared a painful punishment﴾ (76:31).

Then the Almighty says:

﴿On the Day when their tongues, their hands and their feet will bear witness against them concerning what they used to do.﴾ (24)

We all know that it is the tongue that speaks. So what does the verse add with His words ﴿On the Day when their tongues bear witness against them..﴾ (24) [An-Nur]? They say: In this world the tongue speaks and utters, but the real speaker is you, because it moves only by your will for it. The tongue is thus an instrument subject to your will; it is merely a tool. In the Hereafter, however, the tongue will speak against the will of its owner, because its owner will have no will at that time.

To bring this matter closer: do you not see how an intelligent, eloquent man may be struck dumb and lose the power of speech after his fluency, because of an illness or the like, so that he is no longer able to speak, while he is still in the breadth of this world? What has happened? Merely that the instrument of speech has ceased to function in him. Likewise, in the Hereafter your will and your control over all your limbs will cease to function, and they will speak and move, not by your will, but by the will and power of God.

So the meaning of ﴿On the Day when their tongues bear witness against them..﴾ (24) [An-Nur] is: a testimony and a speaking in accordance with the will of God, not in accordance with the will of their owners.

We do not find the speaking of the tongue in this manner far-fetched, for the Exalted has said: ﴿His command, when He intends a thing, is only that He says to it, "Be," and it is.﴾ (82) [Ya-Sin]. He has placed in you, O human being, a model that confirms the truth of this matter. So tell me: what do you do if you wish to stand up from a place right now? By merely intending to stand, you find yourself standing, without thinking about anything, without gathering your strength, your thought, and your muscles; rather, you stand spontaneously, without even knowing the manner of this standing or which muscles moved to perform it.

Compare this smooth, spontaneous movement with the excavator or the great cranes, and how the operator in front of him has a large number of levers and arms, each movement of the machine having a specific arm.

If you have this control and this mastery over yourself and your limbs, how then do you find it far-fetched that your Lord, Mighty and Majestic, should have this control over His creation in the Hereafter?

So the tongue is the place of speech, and it is subject to your will in this world; but in the Hereafter this will is paralysed, and it enters into His saying: ﴿Whose is the dominion today? It is God's, the One, the Subduer.﴾ (16) [Ghafir].

Then He, glorified, says: ﴿and their hands and their feet, concerning what they used to do.﴾ (24) [An-Nur]. These are limbs that had no speech in this world, but they will speak today. The scholars try to bring this matter closer by saying: when a limb performs any action, a picture is taken of it that records what it did, so its speaking on the Day of Resurrection is the appearance of this picture that was taken.

The closest view to all of this is that we say: they truly speak, as He, the Exalted, related about the limbs: ﴿And they will say to their skins, "Why did you testify against us?" They will say, "We were made to speak by God, who made everything speak, and He created you the first time, and to Him you are returned."﴾ (21) [Fussilat].

The meaning of ﴿who made everything speak﴾ is that everything in the universe has a speech suited to it, just as the ant spoke and said: ﴿O ants, enter your dwellings..﴾ (18) [An-Naml], and the hoopoe spoke, saying: ﴿I have encompassed what you have not encompassed, and I have come to you from Sheba with certain news.﴾ (22) [An-Naml].

He, the Exalted, has also said about the speech of these things: ﴿And there is not a thing but that it exalts His praise, but you do not understand their exaltation..﴾ (44) [Al-Isra'].

Yet if God wills for you to understand their speech, He will grant you understanding as He granted Solomon, peace be upon him, who understood from the ant: ﴿So he smiled, laughing at her words..﴾ (19) [An-Naml], just as he understood from the hoopoe, and addressed it on a matter of belief.

And if speech is usually understood through sound, then every creature has its own speech which its kind understands. Therefore we now hear, with the advance of the sciences, of a language for fish, and a language for bees, and so on.

We have said earlier that those who claim among the miracles of the Prophet (ﷺ) that the pebbles glorified God in his hand should correct this expression. Say: "The Messenger of God (ﷺ) heard the pebbles glorifying God in his hand." Otherwise, the pebbles glorify God in the hand of the Prophet (ﷺ), just as they glorify God in the hand of Abu Jahl.

And if you were to ask these limbs: "Why did you testify against me, when it was you who acted?" they would say to you: "We acted because we were subjugated to your will, under your compulsion. But on the day we are released from your will and freed from your compulsion, we will say nothing but the truth."

Then the Truth, glorified is He, says:

﴿On that Day Allah will pay them their due recompense in truth, and they will know that Allah is the Manifest Truth.﴾ (24:25)

His saying ﴿On that Day﴾: that is, the day when this testimony takes place, which is the Day of Resurrection. ﴿Allah will pay them their due recompense in truth﴾: "din" (dīn) is applied to the way (manhaj) of Allah for guiding creation, is applied to the Day of Resurrection, and is applied to recompense (jazā').

So the meaning is: He will pay them the recompense they deserve, ﴿in truth﴾, that is, with justice in which there is no wrong and no alteration. The recompense is not arbitrary (jazāfan); rather it is recompense in truth, because no repentance has come from them and no renewal of faith. Therefore what we warned them of and informed them of, the punishment, must befall them, and there is no other god who could change this ruling or delay it for them.

Therefore, after He, may He be exalted, said:

﴿Perish the hands of Abu Lahab, and perish he! His wealth did not avail him, nor what he gained. He will burn in a Fire of blazing flame, and his wife, the carrier of firewood, around her neck a rope of palm fiber.﴾ (111:1–5)

After that He said:

﴿Say: He is Allah, the One. Allah, the Eternal Refuge. He neither begets nor is born, nor is there to Him any equivalent.﴾ (112:1–4)

That is: there is no other god who could change this statement; what I have said will certainly come to pass.

Then He, may He be exalted, says: ﴿And they will know that Allah is the Manifest Truth﴾ (24:25). And ﴿the Truth﴾ (al-ḥaqq) is the thing that is established and does not change; everything other than Allah, may He be exalted, is changeable. Therefore, Allah, with all the attributes of perfection that are in Him, is free of change, may He be glorified. Thus it is said: Allah, may He be exalted, does not change for our sake, but we must change for the sake of Allah, as He, glorified is He, said: ﴿Indeed, Allah does not change the condition of a people until they change what is in themselves﴾ (13:11).

So Allah is the established Truth. This is known through rational proofs and through reality. We have known many rational proofs. As for reality, until now there has not appeared anyone who says "I am God" and claims this universe for himself, and a claimant's claim is established for him if no one opposes it. The meaning of ﴿the Manifest﴾ (al-mubīn) is: the clear and evident one, whose truth encompasses all existence.

1 Abu Lahab: he is ʿAbd al-ʿUzzá ibn ʿAbd al-Muṭṭalib ibn Hāshim, a Qurashī, uncle of the Messenger of Allah (ﷺ), among the greatest of people in enmity toward the Muslims. He was wealthy and arrogant. It weighed heavily on him to follow the religion that his nephew brought, so he harmed the Muslims, incited against them and fought them. He had a reddish, radiant face, so he was nicknamed Abu Lahab (father of the flame) in the Jahiliyyah. He died a few days after the Battle of Badr, in the year 2 AH. [al-Aʿlām by al-Zirikli 4/12].

2 She is Umm Jamil, whose name was Arwá bint Ḥarb ibn Umayya, and she was a sister of Abu Sufyan. She was a helper to her husband Abu Lahab in his disbelief, obstinacy and stubbornness, therefore on the Day of Resurrection she will be a helper against him in his punishment in the Fire of Hell: she will carry firewood and throw it upon her husband to increase him in what he is in. [Said by Ibn Kathir in his tafsir 4/564].

The Almighty then says:

﴿Evil women are for evil men, and evil men are for evil women; good women are for good men, and good men are for good women. Those are cleared of what they say; for them is forgiveness and a generous provision.﴾ [24:26]

We said in the interpretation of ﴿The fornicator does not marry except a fornicatress or an idolatress, and the fornicatress is not married except by a fornicator or an idolater...﴾ [24:3] that marriage is founded on equality (takafu') so that neither party looks down upon the other. Among this equality is the Exalted One's words: ﴿Evil women are for evil men, and evil men are for evil women; good women are for good men, and good men are for good women...﴾ [24:26].

Then He says: ﴿Those...﴾ [24:26]: that is, those who were involved in the incident of the slander (ifk), about whom people spoke, namely 'A'isha and Safwan. ﴿are cleared of what they say...﴾ [24:26]: that is, of what is said about them. The proof is this equality which the verse mentions. Who is purer than the Messenger of Allah (ﷺ)? As we mentioned, Allah the Exalted would not deceive His Messenger (ﷺ) and make among his wives one around whom doubts hover.

Therefore it must be that 'A'isha is good, a goodness that matches and is suited to the goodness of the Messenger of Allah (ﷺ). For this reason Allah cleared her of what the slanderers say.

As for His words: ﴿for them is forgiveness and a generous provision﴾ [24:26]: forgiveness that descended from the heavens before the Resurrection, and a generous provision. It is true that all provision is from Allah with generosity, but here what is meant is the immaterial provision of honour, rank and exaltedness, not the material provision that sustains the body with food, drink and the like.

Then the Blessed and Exalted Truth says:

﴿O you who have believed, do not enter houses other than your own until you have asked permission and greeted their occupants. That is better for you; perhaps you will be reminded.﴾ (24:27)

The word bayt (house): from it we understand that it is what is prepared for spending the night, where a person takes refuge at the end of the day and rests from the hardship of the day. It is also called dar (dwelling), because it revolves around a place that is specifically yours. Therefore, in the past people lived only in separate private houses, with no sharing in them, unlike apartment buildings today. They would say: "A house with its own door," meaning that no one enters or leaves upon you. Living in this manner was a safeguard against suspicion, because it is your private house, belonging to your family alone, with no one sharing it with them.

However, there are matters that require people to enter upon other people. Therefore, the Truth, Blessed and Exalted, speaks here about the etiquette of seeking permission and the principles and systems that organize this matter, because entering houses without these etiquettes and without observing these systems causes matters that invite suspicion and doubt. Therefore, among the peasants even now: if they see a stranger entering an alley (hara) (2) with which he has no connection, he must be asked: "Why did he enter here?"

So, the law of God does not deprive society of meeting one another; rather, it sets for this meeting limits and etiquettes that negate the suspicion and doubt that could arise in such matters.

Therefore the Almighty and Exalted says, concerning the etiquette of seeking permission: ﴿O you who have believed, do not enter houses other than your own until you have asked permission and greeted their occupants...﴾ (24:27)

﴿Until you have asked permission...﴾ (24:27): from intimacy (anas) and reassurance. When you are sitting with your family in your house, and a stranger you do not know approaches you, if he does not offer you something to be at ease with, such as conversation or a request for permission, then estrangement and aversion will inevitably arise from him. Therefore: the one seeking permission should make a sound that the owner of the house feels at ease with, as we say: "O people of God!", or knock on the door, or speak with a young child so that he informs whoever is in the house.

This is because houses have their sanctity, and every house has its private matters that the owner of the house does not like anyone to see, either out of honor for the owner of the house or out of honor for the visitor himself. Seeking permission makes everyone avoid what would harm him.

Therefore, the Exalted said after it: ﴿That is better for you...﴾ (24:27): that is, better for everyone, for the visitor and the visited. Seeking permission prevents anyone from spying on anyone, and prevents anyone from looking at something that would harm him. Suppose a wife's father wanted to visit her and entered upon her suddenly, and found her in a quarrel with her husband; he might then have seen matters that would not please him, and the disagreement would worsen.

Then the verse concludes with His saying: ﴿Perhaps you will be reminded.﴾ (24:27): that is, beware of neglecting these etiquettes or being lax about them, like those who say, "We are family or relatives, there is no formality between us," for God, who legislated these etiquettes for you, knows what is in your souls and knows what is good for you.

Rather, this Islamic etiquette extends from the stranger to the owner of the house himself. In the noble hadith: "He forbade that a traveler surprise his family at night" (3). Rather, he must inform them of his arrival so that he does not catch them by surprise, and so that each of them may prepare to meet the other.

Then Allah, glorified is He, says:

﴿And if you find no one therein, then do not enter until permission is given to you. And if you are told, "Go back," then go back. That is purer for you. And Allah is Knowing of what you do.﴾ (24:28)

If you ask permission to enter a house in which there is no one, do not enter, because you have come seeking the one who dwells there, not the place itself, unless you intend to enter in order to pry into people's affairs and spy on them.

As for His saying, ﴿until permission is given to you...﴾ (24:28): How (can permission be given) when the house has no one in it?

It may be that the owner of the house is outside it, and when he sees you asking permission he calls out to you from afar: "Come in." So permission must come from the owner of the house or from one who acts on his behalf in giving permission, for he would not grant permission unless he was assured that the way is clear of anything that would harm you or harm the people of the house.

Then He, glorified is He, says: ﴿And if you are told, "Go back," then go back. That is purer for you...﴾ (24:28): Because if you insist on entering after he has said to you, "Go back," you have already raised suspicion in his soul. So you must comply and respect the wishes of the person concerned. This is the purer and better course. Do you not see the saying of the Messenger of Allah (ﷺ): "Leave what makes you doubtful for what does not make you doubtful" (1)?

﴿And Allah is Knowing of what you do.﴾ (24:28): That is, Allah, glorified is He, knows the secrets of hearts and the whisperings of breasts. If the owner of the house says to you, "Go back," and you stand before the door and do not leave, you are stirring up suspicions and illusions around you, while your Lord, Mighty and Majestic, wants to protect you from suspicions and the secrets of souls.

(1) Narrated by Abu Dawud al-Tayalisi in his Musnad (1178), Imam Ahmad in his Musnad (1/200), and al-Tirmidhi in his Sunan (2518), who said: "Hasan sahih hadith," from the hadith of al-Hasan ibn Ali, may Allah be pleased with them both, and its completion is: "Indeed, truthfulness is tranquility, and indeed, lying is doubt."

Then Allah, glorified is He, says:

﴿There is no blame upon you for entering houses other than inhabited ones in which there is provision for you. And Allah knows what you reveal and what you conceal.﴾ (24:29)

Abu Bakr al-Siddiq (may Allah be pleased with him) asked the Messenger of Allah (ﷺ): "O Messenger of Allah, we are a people of trade. We travel to lands where we have no houses or family, and we are obliged to stay in public places (such as hostels) where we place our goods and spend the night." So this verse was revealed.

﴿Blame (junah)...﴾ (24:29): means sin or wrongdoing (ithm aw haraj). This is specific to public places that no particular person inhabits. A public place has rules of entry different from the rules for homes and private places. So do you ask permission to enter a hotel, a commercial shop, or a bathhouse, etc.? These are places in which you bear no blame for entering without seeking permission.

The meaning of ﴿other than inhabited...﴾ (24:29): that is, not for specific people. ﴿in which there is provision for you...﴾ (24:29): such as sleeping in it, eating, drinking, and placing your belongings. Thus "provision" here is not absolute; it is restricted to what Allah has permitted and commanded, so prohibited things do not fall under "provision."

Therefore He says after it: ﴿And Allah knows what you reveal and what you conceal.﴾ (24:29): that is, in determining enjoyment, so do not take it in its absolute sense, lest you include the forbidden. Otherwise, prostitutes frequently frequent such places; therefore your Lord protects you and gives you the necessary immunity for your protection.
