(3) Diwan of Kuthayyir (p. 207), and cited by Shihab al-Din al-Halabi (d. 725 AH) in "Husn al-Tawassul ila Sina'at al-Tarassul," p. 121. Aqza'at al-ghamamah: the cloud was uncovered and went away.
(4) al-Safwan: the smooth stone unsuitable for cultivation (al-Qamus al-Qawim 1/380).
(5) al-Wabl: heavy rain of large drops. And al-Wabil: very heavy and thick (Lisan al-Arab, root: w-b-l).
(6) al-Sald: the hard, smooth stone that is not suitable for growing plants (al-Qamus al-Qawim 1/381).
(7) Mentioned by al-'Ajluni in Kashf al-Khafa' (hadith no. 2618) from Anas ibn Malik, may Allah be pleased with him, and its complete form: "Remember death often, for if you remember it in wealth, it will sour it for you, and if you remember it in hardship, it will widen it for you. Death is the Resurrection; whoever dies, his resurrection has come." It was also related by al-Daylami in Musnad al-Firdaws (hadith 1117) from Anas, raised to the Prophet with the wording: "When one of you dies, his resurrection has come, so worship Allah as if you see Him, and seek His forgiveness every hour."

Next, the Exalted says:

﴿Or [their deeds are] like darkness in a deep sea, covered by waves, above which are waves, above which are clouds: darknesses, some upon others. When he extends his hand, he can hardly see it. And whoever Allah does not grant light, for him there is no light.﴾

This is another illustrative example of the deeds of those who disbelieve. The baḥr lujjī (deep, vast sea) is the wide, great sea in which the waves surge, one upon another, and above all of that are clouds. So the darkness is total (muṭbaq), because it consists of successive layers, in far depths. This darkness has reached such a degree that a person cannot see, within it, even his own hand, which is a part of him; so what of other things?

As for His saying ﴿lam yakad yarāhā…﴾ (24:40): meaning, he does not come close to seeing it. When the nearness to seeing is negated, seeing is negated all the more so (min bāb awlā), because he has no light from Allah by which he sees and is guided. ﴿Whoever Allah does not grant light, for him there is no light﴾ (24:40): just as he has not benefited from light, and did not see even his own hand, so too he does not benefit from anything of his deeds.

Commentary of al-Sha'rawi (Tafsir al-Sha'rawi, surahs 1-53, fragments of 54-66) on surah 24, verse 41:

Then the Truthful, glorified is He, says:

﴿Have you not seen that to Allah glorify whoever is in the heavens and the earth, and the birds in flight? Each has known its prayer and its exaltation. And Allah is Knowing of what they do.﴾

The Real, glorified and exalted is He, wants to draw our attention to what points to the oneness of the Supreme Creator, the perfection of His self-subsistence (qayyumiyyah), and the perfection of His power. This verse came after a number of commands and prohibitions, as if your Lord, mighty and majestic, wants to reassure you that this universe, which He created for your sake, and which was prepared before you were born, indeed before Allah created Adam, was made ready to receive you with its heavens and its earth, its sun and its moon, its water and its air. Your Lord says to you: Be at ease, for nothing in this universe will depart from your service, since it has been subjected to you, and there will never come a day when it rebels or disobeys the commands of Allah:

﴿Have you not seen that to Allah glorify whoever is in the heavens and the earth...﴾ (al-Nur, 41).

﴿Have you not seen...﴾ (al-Nur, 41): meaning, "Do you not know," as in His saying: ﴿Have you not seen how your Lord dealt with the companions of the elephant?﴾ (al-Fil, 1). It is well known that the Prophet (ﷺ) was born in the Year of the Elephant and did not witness that event, so why did his Lord not address him with "Do you not know," and thus ease the minds of people who raise doubts about the wording?

They said: It is to show you that what Allah informs you of, which is unseen to you, is more certain than what your eyes inform you of when it is witnessed before you, because the source of your knowledge is Allah. Do you not see that sight itself may suffer an illness so that its perception becomes disordered, like someone who has color blindness or short-sightedness... etc. So then: sight itself, which is the most certain thing you have, may deceive.

Tasbih (glorification) is tanzih (declaring transcendence), and tanzih means that you elevate the one being declared transcendent above the level of what might occur to your mind. Allah, the Exalted, has existence, and you have existence, but the existence of Allah is not like your existence. Allah has an essence and attributes, but they are not like your essence and attributes... etc.

So then: declare the essence of Allah transcendent above the essences you know, for those are essences that were granted existence, whereas the essence of Allah is not granted; the essence of Allah is self-existent. Likewise you have an act, and Allah, the Exalted, has an act.

We have mentioned in His saying: ﴿Glory be to Him who took His servant by night from al-Masjid al-Haram to al-Masjid al-Aqsa...﴾ (al-Isra', 1).

Those who objected to this act objected out of stupidity, for they did not distinguish between the act of Allah and the act of the servant. The Messenger of Allah (ﷺ) did not say: "I traveled from Mecca to Jerusalem," but rather said: "I was taken by night (usri bi)."

So objecting to this is a sophistry. If you strike camels' livers for a month to reach it, that is because your travel is subject to your power and capabilities, whereas Allah, the Exalted, says to a thing: "Be," and it is, so He needs no time in His act, glorified is He. Thus it is part of good manners not to compare the act of Allah with your act, and part of good manners to declare Allah transcendent above everything that occurs to your mind. Declare Allah transcendent in His essence, declare Him transcendent in His attributes, and declare Him transcendent in His acts.

Do you not see that "subhan" (glory be) is a verbal noun for tasbih, which shows that Allah's transcendence is established for Him, glorified is He, before He created anyone to declare Him transcendent, as in His saying: ﴿Allah bears witness that there is no deity except Him...﴾ (Al 'Imran, 18). The Real, blessed and exalted, bore witness to Himself before you bore witness, and before the angels bore witness; this is the witness of the Essence to the Essence. And before Allah created the human being who glorifies, the heavens and the earth glorified Allah at the moment He created them, glorified and exalted is He.

When you trace the wording of tasbih in the Noble Qur'an, you find that it came once in the past tense: ﴿Whatever is in the heavens and the earth glorifies Allah...﴾ (al-Hadid, 1). Did the heavens and the earth glorify once, then say "Glory be to Allah," and then fall silent from glorification? No, they glorified in the past, and they still glorify in the present: ﴿Whatever is in the heavens and whatever is in the earth glorifies Allah...﴾ (al-Jumu'ah, 1).

Since the whole universe glorifies Allah, and still glorifies, there remains only you, O son of Adam: ﴿Glorify the name of your Lord, the Most High﴾ (al-A'la, 1). That is: be ashamed that the whole universe glorifies while you do not glorify; join your glorification to the glorification of all these creatures.

It is strange that we hear someone say that "man" (min) in the verse refers to the rational being, that it is the rational one who glorifies, while the heavens and the earth have no part in this matter. We say: they have no part in your conception, but in reality they glorify just as you do, as He, the Exalted, said: ﴿Each has known its prayer and its exaltation...﴾ (al-Nur, 41).

And He said: ﴿And thunder glorifies Him with His praise, and the angels out of fear of Him...﴾ (al-Ra'd, 13). So after the speech of Allah, there is no speech left for you.

Another says to you: The glorification here is not literal; it is glorification by indication and state, not by speech. That is, these creatures by their condition point to the glorification of Allah and His transcendence, and that He is One with no partner, in line with the poet's saying: "And in everything He has a sign, which points to His being the One."

This view is refuted by His saying: ﴿There is nothing that does not glorify Him with His praise, but you do not understand their glorification...﴾ (al-Isra', 44).

So these creatures glorify in reality, and they have a tongue and a language, but you do not understand from them and do not comprehend their languages. Have you understood all the languages of your own kind, so that you could understand the languages of other creatures? If an Arab does not learn English, for example, he cannot understand anything from it, though it is a spoken and written language with words, expressions and structures like Arabic.

So: do not say it is glorification of state; it is glorification of speech, but you do not understand it, and everything that has speech knows its speech. The proof is that Allah, if He wills, lets some of the chosen ones know these languages, so they understand them, as Solomon (peace be upon him) understood the ant: ﴿So he smiled, laughing at her speech...﴾ (al-Naml, 19). And he heard the speech of the hoopoe and understood from it what it said about the queen of Sheba.

We say to the proponents of this view: Reflect on the hexagonal cell that bees construct, and the geometry in it that challenges the masters of geometry and measurement to make its like. Reflect on the nest of a bird and how it weaves straws, interlacing them, and makes a rim for the nest to protect the young; when you put your hand into a nest made of straw, you find it has the feel of silk. Reflect on the threads of the spider and how it catches its prey with them.

I once watched a filmed documentary recording a struggle between a bear and a bull. The bear saw the bull's horns, long and sharp, and knew they were the bull's means of destroying it, so it charged the bull, seized its horns with its paws, and kept tearing at the bull's head with its teeth until it had inflicted wounds on it, until it fell, and then it began to eat it.

So: how do we find it unlikely that these creatures have languages with which they glorify Allah, which only their own kind knows, or those upon whom Allah has bestowed knowledge of them?

Then, did man not learn from the crow how to bury the dead when Qabil killed Habil? As He, glorified is He, says: ﴿Then Allah sent a crow scratching in the earth to show him how to conceal the corpse of his brother...﴾ (al-Ma'idah, 31). It is as if our Lord, mighty and majestic, is teaching us manners and freedom from conceit.

We have read that some researchers and students of the life of ants found that it forms a complete kingdom that has reached the peak of order and cooperation. They observed a group passing here and there, until they found a piece of food; they left it and departed, returning whence they came. Then came after them a troop of ants that surrounded this piece, carried it to the nest. Then the researcher placed another piece twice the size of the first, and behold, the exploring group (or the "scout" group) passed over it and went on without trying to carry it. After that came a group of ants twice the size of the first group. It is as if the ants know volume, weight and mass and are skilled at estimating them.

On one occasion the researcher noticed a white grain in front of an ant nest. When he examined it, he found it was the embryo of a seed that would become a plant. The ants had found a way to separate this embryo so that the seed would not sprout and collapse the nest upon them. To this degree the ants know the law of their preservation, and know how to protect themselves, though they are among the smallest of creatures. After all this, do we find it unlikely that ants, or others, have their own language?

Then He, glorified is He, says: ﴿And the birds in flight. Each has known its prayer and its exaltation...﴾ (al-Nur, 41). So why did He single out the birds for mention, though they are included in ﴿whoever is in the heavens and the earth...﴾ (al-Nur, 41)?

They said: He singled them out because they have another distinctive and wondrous characteristic that we must pay attention to, for Allah, the Exalted, wants to make the bird an example and model of something greater. The bird is a creature that has weight and mass, subject to the law of gravity, which pulls to the earth every weight suspended in the air.

But the Real, glorified and exalted is He, breaks this law for the bird when it spreads its wings in the air; it remains suspended and does not fall: ﴿Have they not seen the birds above them, spreading their wings and folding them? None holds them up except the Most Merciful...﴾ (al-Mulk, 19).

It is as if the Creator, mighty and majestic, is saying: Take from the visible bird a model and a means of illustration. So when I tell you: ﴿And He holds back the sky from falling upon the earth, except by His permission...﴾ (al-Hajj, 65), then believe and affirm that Allah holds up the sky. Indeed: ﴿Allah holds the heavens and the earth lest they cease; and if they should cease, none could hold them after Him...﴾ (Fatir, 41).

So take from the scene you perceive a proof of what you do not perceive.

But who is the agent in ﴿Each has known its prayer and its exaltation...﴾ (al-Nur, 41)?

It may be that the agent is the birds and everything in existence; and better than this is to say: Allah knows their prayer and their glorification, because He, glorified is He, is their Creator and the One who guides them to this glorification (1). So everything in existence knows its prayer and knows its glorification, just as you know the method, but it remains upright on its method because it is subjected, while you have deviated because you have been given choice.

If you wish your life's affairs to be set right, then apply the method of Allah as it came to you. Therefore you will find no defect in the universe at all except in the realm of human choice. Everything in which man has no part runs in an orderly fashion: the sun has never once in days past opposed or fallen behind, and likewise the moon, the stars and the air; they are governed with utmost regularity, to the extent that people set their calculations, appointments and directions by them.

Therefore He, the Exalted, says: ﴿The sun and the moon follow a precise reckoning﴾ (al-Rahman, 5). That is: by exact calculation. The sun could not regulate time unless it were itself regulated in its essence.

﴿And Allah is Knowing of what they do﴾ (al-Nur, 41): that is, because of His self-subsistence over His creation.

1 Al-Qurtubi said in his tafsir (6/4824): "It is permissible that the meaning be: each has known Allah's prayer and His glorification, that is, He knows the prayer of the one who prays and the glorification of the one who glorifies; and for this reason He said: ﴿And Allah is Knowing of what they do﴾ (al-Nur, 41), that is, their obedience and their glorification are not hidden from Him. It has also been said that the meaning is: each one who prays and glorifies knows the prayer of his own self and its glorification, which he has been charged with."

Then Allah, glorified and exalted, says:

﴿And to Allah belongs the dominion of the heavens and the earth, and to Allah is the final return.﴾

Your Lord, Mighty and Majestic, wants to reassure you that the One who has charged you with what He has charged you with guarantees for you the means of your life. The air will never be cut off from you on any day, and the sun, the moon, and the earth will not refuse to serve you, because they belong to Allah, and none shares with Him in their ownership to withhold them from you. So be at peace that they will perform their task of serving you until the Day of Resurrection, and do not preoccupy yourself with them, for Allah has guaranteed them.

Then the Lord of Might, glory be to Him, says:

﴿Have you not seen that Allah drives the clouds gently, then joins them together, then makes them into layers, so that you see the rain come forth from their midst? And He sends down from the sky mountains [of clouds] wherein is hail, and strikes with it whom He wills and averts it from whom He wills. The flash of its lightning nearly takes away the sight.﴾ [24:43]

His saying, the Exalted: ﴿Have you not seen…﴾ [24:43]: That is, have you not known. We have already paused with the development of science regarding how rain forms between evaporation and the condensation that becomes cloud. We said previously that the surface of water on the earth is three-quarters of the land, so that this area suffices for the evaporation necessary for rain to occur. We perform a similar process when distilling water: we boil water and receive the vapour on a cold surface, and condensation takes place for it.

We have explained this process with a glass of water. When you leave it full and travel, for example, when you return you find the glass has decreased slightly; but if you spill it on the ground, it dries quickly, before you leave the place. Why? Because you have widened the surface area for evaporation.

The meaning of ﴿He drives the clouds…﴾ [24:43]: that is, He sends them gently and leisurely. Therefore, when the poet described the walk of the girl, he said: "Her gait from her neighbour's house is like the passing of a cloud, neither delayed nor hurried."

﴿Then joins them together…﴾ [24:43]: that is, He gathers some of it upon some. When a thing is gathered part upon part, a gap must remain between them, so that they do not fully merge with one another. Had it not been for these gaps between pieces of cloud, and these openings, the rain would not have come down from within them.

Had He willed, glory be to Him, He would have made the cloud one single piece; but He, glory be to Him, joins it and gathers it part upon part without unifying it in its formation, so that gaps arise between the pieces of cloud. Have you seen how, when we stick paper with glue for example, however much weight we place on it, gaps must remain between it, because it is not one single substance?

This process of emptying the air is something you observe when you place a wet cup and leave it for a while: the water beneath it evaporates and the air exits; then when you want to lift it you find it difficult. Why? Because the air has been emptied from beneath the base of the cup. Among those who treat pains caused by cold, they place an inverted cup over the place of pain, then ignite a piece of cloth, for example, inside it, to burn the air within the cup.

Thereby we prevent a defect in the contact of the cup with the body. This matter is the secret of the greatness of the ancient Egyptians in building, where stones hold together without any mortar (mūna) binding them.

So: the presence of air between two things creates a defect between them; had it not been for this defect in the clouds, no water would have descended from them. Rain is a great sign of Allah's signs which we do not feel. And you can imagine how much a glass of distilled water costs us when we prepare it in the laboratory; what then of the rain that waters the whole earth?

Then He, the Exalted, says: ﴿Then makes them into layers…﴾ [24:43]: that is, piled one upon another. And in another verse: ﴿And if they see a fragment of the sky falling, they say, "Layered cloud"﴾ [52:44], piled up one upon another. ﴿Then you see the rain…﴾ [24:43]: that is, the rain ﴿comes forth from within it…﴾ [24:43]: that is, from within these openings and gaps that separate the clouds.

This water that descends from the sky, by which Allah gives life to the earth, may come as vengeance and punishment, as He, glory be to Him, said: ﴿And He sends down from the sky mountains [of clouds] wherein is hail, and strikes with it whom He wills and averts it from whom He wills…﴾ [24:43]. For us, in the people of Ma'rib whom Allah drowned, there is a lesson and an admonition.

If you reflect, you will find water and fire to be two opposing enemies that are hard to resist; therefore the Arabs, until recent times, feared water because they had witnessed drowning after the collapse of the Ma'rib Dam; so they preferred to live in the desert, far from water.

With water Allah, the Exalted, saved Moses, peace be upon him, and drowned his enemy Pharaoh; He, glory be to Him, did the thing and its opposite with one and the same thing.

His saying, the Exalted: ﴿The flash of its lightning nearly takes away the sight﴾ [24:43]: that is, the intense light produced by the cloud nearly snatches away the sight. And in lightning, fire is generated from water; therefore, when He, the Exalted, says: ﴿And when the seas are set ablaze﴾ [81:6], confirm this unseen verse, for you have witnessed a model of it in the matter of lightning.

1 al-wadq: the rain, heavy or light. (Lisan al-'Arab, root w-d-q.)

2 al-sana: the light of fire and of lightning. Abu Zayd said: the sana of lightning is its light without your seeing the lightning itself or seeing its place of emergence; sana occurs only at night, not by day, and may sometimes be without cloud. (Lisan al-'Arab, root s-n-a.)

3 al-rayth: delay. rata yarithu: he delayed; tarayyatha fulan 'alayna: he delayed with us. (Lisan al-'Arab, root r-y-th.)

4 That is, filled with water, or filled with fire on the Day of Resurrection. (al-Qamus al-Qawim 1/303.)

Then the Truthful (al-Haqq), glorified is He, says:

﴿It is Allah who alternates the night and the day. Indeed in that is a lesson for those who have insight.﴾ (24:44)

The night and the day are two signs that follow one another, yet without monotony. The night may take from the day, and the day may take from the night, and they may become exactly equal in length. Among the alternation of the night and the day is what befalls them of heat, cold, light and darkness.

Thus the matter is not a mechanical, monotonous routine; rather it is the self-subsisting power (qayyumiyyah) of Allah, may He be exalted, and His ability to direct affairs according to His will, may He be exalted. Therefore, after this, He says:

﴿Indeed in that is a lesson for those who have insight.﴾ (al-Nur)

The words 'ibrah (lesson), i'tibar (taking a lesson), 'ubur (crossing over) and ta'bir (expression) all derive from one root. We say: "This is a place of 'ubur," meaning passage from one side to another; and "So-and-so 'abbara 'an kadha," meaning he conveyed inner speech into spoken words. And 'ibrah also means that we look at a thing and take a lesson from it, then move on from it to something else. Likewise, 'abrah (tears) is a grief that has made something flow, so that tears fall from the eye.

And for whom is the lesson here? ﴿For those who have insight (ulu al-absar)﴾ (al-Nur). What is meant is the perceiving sight that comprehends, not the sight that merely perceives. A human being has perceptions through their means, and has an intellect that receives what is perceived, sifts it, and draws from it conclusions. Among people is one who sees but sees nothing and gains nothing from his seeing, and among them are the possessors of conscious, precise observation. The one who discovered the power of steam saw the cooking pot boiling and bubbling, and the lid rising over it. This is a sight we all see, man and woman, old and young, but no one arrived at what he arrived at.

Thus what is meant is the sight that conveys the observed to the intellect so that it may analyze it and deduce from it the causes within it, perhaps benefiting from it in something that profits him. Allah, may He be exalted, has created in the universe phenomena and signs which, if a person reflects upon them and looks at them with understanding and insight, he would deduce from them what enriches his life and elevates it.

Commentary of al-Sha'rawi (Tafsir al-Sha'rawi, surahs 1-53, fragments of 54-66) on surah 24, verse 45:

Then the Truth, glorified is He, says:

﴿And Allah has created every creature (dābba) from water. Of them are some that walk on their bellies, and of them are some that walk on two legs, and of them are some that walk on four. Allah creates what He wills; indeed Allah is competent over all things.﴾

Al-dābba (creature): everything that crawls upon the earth, whether human, livestock or wild beast. Every creature that moves upon the earth Allah created from water, even the ant, which has its own crawling upon the earth.

Everything that is magnified is capable of being made small, and it may be magnified to such a degree that you cannot grasp its reality, and it may be made so small that you can hardly see it, needing a magnifier to see it. Among the wonders of creation is that the ant or the mosquito contains all the apparatus and essentials of life, and it has a life like the life of the huge elephant. From the greatness of the Creator, glorified is He, is that He creates a huge thing that exceeds perception in its enormity, and creates a tiny thing that exceeds perception in its minuteness.

Do you not see that the watch of "Big Ben" gained its fame from the enormity of its size, and then after that there came a watch made in the size of a ring's bezel, containing the very same mechanisms as the Big Ben watch? Likewise Allah created from water the huge elephant, and created the mosquito that disturbs the elephant despite its smallness... Glory be to the Creator.

Since water is the origin in the creation of every living thing, we find scholars killing even the tiny, minute microbe by withholding watery medium from it, so it dies. Among this is treating wounds with honey, because it absorbs moisture or withholds it, so the microbe finds no watery medium in which to live.

And this creation is not of one form, nor of one pattern in fixed moulds; rather it is varieties and forms: ﴿Of them are some that walk on their bellies, and of them are some that walk on two legs, and of them are some that walk on four...﴾ (al-Nur).

Mashy (walking): is the transfer of the thing described as walking from one place to another place. People understand walking to be only by the two feet, but the Almighty makes clear to us that walking has kinds: among creatures are those that walk on their bellies, those that walk on two legs, and those that walk on four.(1)

Our Lord, glorified and exalted is He, has spread out this matter in a manner that suits the inimitability of the Qur'an and its conciseness. He did not mention, for example, that among creatures there are some with forty-four legs; yet in the variety of walking methods among creatures there are wonders that show us His power, exalted is He, and the originality of His creation.

Therefore He said after it: ﴿Allah creates what He wills...﴾ (al-Nur), because the verse did not exhaust all forms of walking; rather it gives us examples. Under ﴿Allah creates what He wills...﴾ (al-Nur) falls, for example, "the one with forty-four" (umm arba'a wa-arba'īn) and other creatures, and the verse is evidence of the absoluteness of His power, glorified is He.

Just as man has been subjected to serve man, so too livestock has been subjected to serve livestock, to provide for it the essentials of its life. Do you not see the bird that feeds on food leftovers between the teeth of the crocodile, for example, cleaning them for it? So what is in the crocodile's mouth of residues and bacteria is a storehouse of sustenance for these birds, and there arises between them harmony, accord and cooperation, to the extent that if the bird sees the hunter who wants to catch the crocodile, it makes a sound to alert the crocodile so that it escapes.

Among walking is also going about among people with slander (namīma), as Almighty God said: ﴿Constant slanderer, going about with gossip﴾ (al-Qalam).

1 Al-Naqqash said: He suffices in mentioning what walks on four rather than mentioning what walks on more, because the foundation of all animals' locomotion is on four, which is the basis of their walking, and the abundance of legs in some is an addition to their creation, which that animal does not need in its walking, all of them. Ibn 'Atiyya said: The apparent meaning is that those many legs are not in vain; rather the animal needs them to move, and they all move in its management. (Tafsir al-Qurtubi 6/4829).
2 Al-hammaz: an intensive form. Al-hamaza: one who frequently defames, backbites, insults and disparages people. It is said that "al-hamz" is in the back and in secret, and "al-mazz" is a defect in the face openly. (al-Qamus al-Qawim 2/307).

Commentary of al-Sha'rawi (Tafsir al-Sha'rawi, surahs 1-53, fragments of 54-66) on surah 24, verse 46:

After Allah, blessed and exalted is He, has given us the proofs that dominion belongs to Him alone, that everything glorifies Him, that all matters return to Him, and that He created every creature from water, He, glorified is He, said:

﴿We have certainly sent down clear revelations, and Allah guides whom He wills to a straight path.﴾

Meaning: He who alone possesses this dominion and created for you these wonders has sent down for you clear revelations that carry to you the rulings. Just as He has done what is beautiful for you and provided for you what serves you in the universe, its heaven and its earth, so you too must fulfill what is incumbent upon you towards His method and His rulings, and follow these clear revelations.

As for the meaning of ﴿clear...﴾ (al-Nur): that is, for the uprightness of the movement of life, because the movement of life requires that everyone move and perform his task fully, so that the movements support one another and do not contradict one another. What wearies the world is that you build while another demolishes.

Therefore, there must be a value-based regulator (dabit qimi) that governs all movements and urges every craftsman to perfect his craft and be sincere in it. A person generally does well in only one corner of his life, namely his trade and specialization, and perhaps does not do it well for himself, because he is not paid for it. That is why they say, "The carpenter's door is loose" (bab al-najjar mukhala'). But if he works for others, he does his work well and perfects his craft. Likewise, people perfect for you what is in their hands, and affairs become upright. So, the best of what is in your hand, give to people, and people will give you the best of what is in their hands.

As for the Exalted's saying: ﴿And Allah guides whom He wills to a straight path﴾ (al-Nur):

One may ask: What is the fault of the one who did not enter into this will and so was not guided? We have previously said that guidance is of two kinds: guidance of indication (hidayat al-dalala) and guidance of assistance upon indication (hidayat al-ma'huna 'ala al-dalala).

So Allah guides everyone with the guidance of indication, and makes clear to all the causes of good, the paths of salvation, the way to success, and the best method for managing the movement of life. Whoever hears the words of Allah, trusts in His guidance, and obeys, He assists him with the guidance of assistance.

So when you hear: ﴿And Allah does not guide the wicked people﴾ (al-Ma'idah, 108).

﴿And Allah does not guide the wrongdoing people﴾ (al-Baqarah, 258).

Know that they refused the guidance of indication, so the guidance of assistance was withheld from them, not the guidance of indication, clarification and direction.

We have said that the phrase ﴿We have sent down...﴾ (al-Nur) conveys honour to the thing sent down, because sending down (inzal) occurs only from a height to a lower place. It is as if your Lord, mighty and majestic is He, when He assigns you a duty, says to you: "I want to raise you from the level of the earth to the height of the heavens." Therefore, He, exalted is He, says elsewhere: ﴿Say: Come, I will recite what your Lord has forbidden you...﴾ (al-An'am, 151).

That is: do not set down laws for yourselves, and do not follow your opinions and ideas. Rather, come to Allah and take from Him, glorified is He, the method of your life, for He is the One who created you and created for you this life.

Commentary of al-Sha'rawi (Tafsir al-Sha'rawi, surahs 1-53, fragments of 54-66) on surah 24, verse 47:

Then the Truthful (al-Haqq) (subhanahu) says:

{They say, "We believe in Allah and the Messenger, and we obey," then a faction of them turn away after that. And those are not believers.} [24:47]

In another verse He (subhanahu) says: ﴿And when it is said to them, "Come to what Allah has revealed and to the Messenger," you see the hypocrites turning away from you with aversion.﴾ [4:61] These are the hypocrites. The misfortune of the hypocrite is that his psychological faculties are in conflict (mutaḍārib al-malakāt al-nafsiyya). This is because a human being has several faculties (malakāt), which support one another when he is upright and oppose one another when he is in disobedience. You see a person behaving naturally when he looks at his daughter or his wife, because his faculties are in harmony with this act. But when he looks at the women who are forbidden to him (maḥārim al-ghayr), you see him stealing a glance, fearing that someone will see him spying, and taking precautions, because his faculties are disturbed and not in harmony with this act.

Therefore they say: "Uprightness (al-istiqāma) is [a matter of] being pleasing (al-istisāma)" (1). The faculties of the soul, by their nature, support one another and never conflict. But the hypocrite, in addition to his lying, has conflicting faculties within himself, because his heart is disbelieving while his tongue is believing.

Therefore a person's dignity lies first between him and his own self before it lies between him and people. A person may do good deeds in front of people that impress others, yet he knows the evil in himself. Even if he wins the trust of the society around him, he has lost his own opinion of himself in himself. When a person loses himself, nothing will compensate him for it, even if he gains the whole world; for society is not with you all the time, whereas your self is with you all the time and never leaves you. I am great in front of people as long as I am with them, but when I am alone with myself I find it contemptible: "I did such-and-such, and I did such-and-such."

So: you have judged that people's opinion of you is more precious than your own opinion. Had your opinion of yourself had any value for you, you would have tried to make your opinion of yourself correct. But you want people's opinion of you to be correct, even if your opinion of yourself is otherwise.

The Exalted says about these people: ﴿Have you not seen those who claim that they believe in what has been revealed to you and what was revealed before you, yet desire to refer their disputes to the false deity (ṭāghūt), though they were commanded to reject it? And Satan wants to lead them far astray.﴾ [4:60]

He has judged that they "claim" (yazʿumūn), and claim is the mount of lying. The proof that they are claiming is that they desire to refer their disputes to the ṭāghūt; had they truly believed in what was revealed to you and what was revealed before you, they would not have referred to the ṭāghūt. Thus they exposed themselves: the second clause exposed the first.

Therefore they said: "The disbeliever is better than them, because his faculties are consistent: his heart agrees with his tongue; his heart is disbelieving and his tongue is likewise." That is why the hypocrites are in the lowest level of the Fire.

The Almighty, blessed and exalted, gives us an image and a model warning us not to judge a statement by itself alone. He says about the hypocrites: ﴿When the hypocrites come to you, they say, "We testify that you are indeed the Messenger of Allah." And Allah knows that you are His Messenger, and Allah testifies that the hypocrites are liars.﴾ [63:1]

This statement, ﴿"You are indeed the Messenger of Allah..."﴾ [63:1], is a true statement, but the Qur'an denies them in that they testified to it.

These two verses (2) were revealed concerning one of the hypocrites, whom I think was Bishr (3), who had a dispute with a Jew. The Jew asked that they go to judgment before the Messenger of Allah (ṣallā Allāh ʿalayhi wa-sallam), and the hypocrite asked that they go to judgment before Ka'b (ibn al-Ashraf), because of what he knew of his deceit and lack of trustworthiness. (A person, even if he is corrupt in himself, must still submit his affair to the trustworthy and just.) Indeed the Jew prevailed, and they went to the Messenger of Allah, and he ruled for the Jew. In this there is an indication that the Jew was intelligent and perceptive, knowing the truth and knowing the station of the Messenger of Allah (ṣallā Allāh ʿalayhi wa-sallam).

But the hypocrite was not content with the ruling of the Messenger of Allah, and the matter ended with them going to ʿUmar (raḍiya Allāh ʿanhu), and they related to him what had happened. When he learned that the hypocrite had rejected the ruling of the Messenger of Allah, ʿUmar rose, took a sword, and brandished it in the face of the hypocrite, saying: "Whoever is not content with the judgment of the Messenger of Allah, then this is my judgment on him."

So: these people say: ﴿"We believe in Allah and the Messenger, and we obey..."﴾ [24:47]. It is a beautiful statement, and may Allah increase the good in you, but it is only a statement not supported by practical application, and faith requires that deeds conform to what faith utters.

So this from them is mere talk. As for the practice: ﴿then a faction of them turn away after that...﴾ [24:47]. Tawallī (turning away) is departing from something that existed toward something contradictory to it. {And those are not believers} [24:47]: since they have turned away, they have neither obeyed nor believed.

(1) One who adorns himself with medals and prefers beauty and goodliness; al-istisāma means seeking goodness and beauty.
(2) He means the two following verses of surah al-Nur, verses 48-49.
(3) This story is reported as the occasion of revelation (sabab al-nuzūl) of another verse: ﴿Have you not seen those who claim that they believe in what has been revealed to you... [4:60]. Al-Wahidi reported it in Asbab al-Nuzul (p. 92) from Ibn ʿAbbas, who said: "It was revealed—i.e., the verse of surah al-Nisa'—concerning a man of the hypocrites who had a dispute with a Jew. The Jew said: 'Let us go to Muhammad.' The hypocrite said: 'Rather, let us go to Ka'b ibn al-Ashraf,' whom Allah named the ṭāghūt. The Jew refused except to dispute before the Messenger of Allah (ṣallā Allāh ʿalayhi wa-sallam). When the hypocrite saw that, he came with him to the Messenger of Allah, and they disputed before him. The Messenger of Allah (ṣallā Allāh ʿalayhi wa-sallam) ruled for the Jew. When they left his presence, the hypocrite clung to him and said: 'Let us go to ʿUmar ibn al-Khaṭṭāb.' So they came to ʿUmar. The Jew said: 'We disputed, I and this man, before Muhammad, and he ruled against him, but he was not content with his judgment, and he claims that he is disputing before you, and he clung to me, so I came to you with him.' ʿUmar said to the hypocrite: 'Is that so?' He said: 'Yes.' He said to them both: 'Wait until I come out to you.' ʿUmar entered, took the sword and wrapped himself in it, then came out to them and struck the hypocrite with it until he was cold, and said: 'Thus I judge for whoever is not content with the judgment of Allah and the judgment of His Messenger.' The Jew fled, and this verse was revealed. Jibril said: 'ʿUmar distinguished between truth and falsehood,' so he was named al-Faruq." He also reported it in Asbab al-Nuzul (p. 188), and al-Qurtubi likewise reported it in his Tafsir (6/4831).

The intended reference is the matter of Bishr and a Jew, and both of them turned away from the judgment of God and His Messenger. Although the hypocrite's turning away is evident, the verse does not intend to absolve the Jew, for he accepted the judgment of God only because he was confident that the right was on his side, and confident that the Messenger of God (ﷺ) would judge only by the truth, even if the one in question were a Jew. Accordingly, he did not submit to the judgment of God and His Messenger out of love for it or faith in it, but for his own personal interest. Therefore the Exalted says afterward: ﴿Is there a disease in their hearts, or have they doubted, or do they fear that God and His Messenger will be unjust to them? Rather, they are the wrongdoers.﴾

¹ Al-ḥayf: inclination in judgment and oppression in it. Ḥāfa yaḥīf: he acted unjustly and oppressed. (Qamus al-Qawim 1/181).

*Repeated text, because it is shared with verse 48:* ﴿And when they are called to God and His Messenger, that He may judge between them, behold, a party of them turn away. But if the right is theirs, they come to him willingly.﴾

The intended reference is the case of Bishr and the Jew, both of whom turned away from the judgment of God and His Messenger. Although the turning away of the hypocrite is clear, the verse does not aim to absolve the Jew. He accepted the judgment of God and His Messenger only because he was confident that the right was on his side, and confident that the Messenger of God (ﷺ) would judge only by the truth, even if the one judged were a Jew. Therefore, he did not submit to the judgment of God and His Messenger out of love for it or faith in it, but only for his own personal benefit. For this reason, God says after it: ﴿Is there a disease in their hearts, or do they have doubt, or do they fear that God and His Messenger will be unjust to them? Rather, it is they who are the wrongdoers.﴾

Footnote 1: *al-ḥayf* (injustice): inclination in judgment and oppression in it. *Ḥāfa, yaḥīfu*: he acted unjustly and oppressed. (Qamus al-Qawim, 1/181).

Commentary of al-Sha'rawi (Tafsir al-Sha'rawi, surahs 1–53, fragments of 54–66) on surah 24, verse 50:

﴿Is there in their hearts a disease, or do they doubt, or do they fear that Allah and His Messenger will wrong them? Rather, they are the wrongdoers.﴾

Al-marad (disease): the departure of a thing from its sound, healthy state. Each of your limbs has a soundness: the eye has its soundness, the ear has its soundness... etc. What is remarkable is that you live with a bodily part without being aware of it as long as it is sound and healthy. But when illness befalls it, you become alert to it and feel the blessing of Allah upon you in it during its soundness.

﴿Or do they doubt...﴾ (al-Nur): meaning, they doubt the Messenger of Allah. ﴿Or do they fear that Allah and His Messenger will wrong them...﴾ (al-Nur): meaning, that He will act unjustly and oppress.

﴿Rather, they are the wrongdoers﴾ (al-Nur): that is, because they harm themselves first. And this is the extreme of foolishness, that a person wrongs himself. If he wronged others, we would say: he brings a benefit to himself. But what benefit is there in a person wronging himself? And whoever wrongs himself, do not blame him if he wrongs others.

When Allah, blessed and exalted is He, punishes the wrongdoer, that is for his own benefit, so that he does not persist in his wrongdoing and bring upon himself the penalty of evil after Allah, glory be to Him, had held out to him the reward of good.

¹ al-Haif: inclination in judgment and injustice in it. Haafa yahif: he acted unjustly and oppressed. (Qamus al-Qawim 1/181).

Then the context brings the contrast:

﴿The only saying of the believers, when they are called to Allah and His Messenger that he may judge between them, is that they say: "We hear and we obey." And those are the successful.﴾ [51]

So, since you have believed, and faith cannot be except by desire and choice, no one compelling you to it, you must respect your own choice by obeying this choice; otherwise you would make foolish your opinion and your choice. Therefore the condition of the believers, when they are called to Allah and His Messenger, is that they say: "We hear and we obey."

If you reflect on the universe around you, you will find it moving upon this rule. Whatever is below man in the dominion of Allah is compelled, not free to choose, although the original state was that he was free to choose first. He chose to be compelled from the beginning and relieved himself, as He, glory be to Him, said: ﴿Indeed, We offered the Trust to the heavens and the earth and the mountains, but they refused to bear it and feared it...﴾ [72].

The opening of the noble verse with (innama, "only") indicates that it was preceded by a counterpart, and this counterpart is the opposite of what comes after it: the hypocrites turned away and rejected the judgment of Allah and His Messenger, while the believers said "We hear and we obey." It is like your saying: "So-and-so is lazy; only his brother is diligent." The saying of the hypocrites is that they do not accept the judgment of Allah and His Messenger, whereas the believers accept the judgment of Allah and His Messenger.

The meaning of ﴿We hear and we obey...﴾ [51] (al-Nur): that is, "We heard with attentive hearing that is followed by response and obedience," not merely that the sound reaches the ear of the listener without anything affecting him.

He, exalted is He, says in another place: ﴿And when they hear what has been revealed to the Messenger, you see their eyes overflow with tears because of what they recognize of the truth...﴾ [83] (al-Ma'idah).

Hearing has a function, and here it means: "We have answered, O Lord, and we are resolved to respond," and this is a verbal promise followed by execution and obedience. Like our saying in prayer: "Allah hears whoever praises Him" (sami' Allahu liman hamidah), meaning: Allah answers whoever praises Him.

﴿And those are the successful [51]﴾ (al-Nur): al-mufliḥun (the successful): those who attain the level of success (al-falah). It is remarkable that the Truth, glory be to Him, uses the word falah (success), which derives from farmers' cultivation of the land (filaha al-ard), because tilling the earth is the foundation of sustenance, and whoever perfects the cultivation of his land, it yields a good fruit, its goodness increases, and its produce is multiplied, to the point that a single grain of wheat gives seven hundred grains. If the earth, which is created by Allah the Exalted, gives those who cultivate it all this bounty, then what of the Creator of the earth, how will His giving be?

Then the Almighty says:

﴿And whoever obeys Allah and His Messenger and fears Allah and is mindful of Him — it is those who are the victorious.﴾ (24:52)

Our master, Shaykh Musa Sharif — may Allah have mercy on him and be pleased with him — used to teach us tafsir. When this verse came up, he said: "Listen, this is a telegram from Allah, the Exalted:
﴿And whoever obeys Allah and His Messenger and fears Allah and is mindful of Him — it is those who are the victorious.﴾ (An-Nur). This verse leaves out no ruling of Islam without including it in this concise telegram, which gathers the entire method."(1)

The meaning of ﴿obeys Allah and His Messenger...﴾ (An-Nur 52): he believes in Allah, obeys Him, and affirms His Messenger. ﴿And fears Allah...﴾ (An-Nur 52): that is, he fears Him for the sins that have passed. ﴿And is mindful of Him﴾ (An-Nur 52): in the remainder of his life. ﴿It is those who are the victorious﴾ (An-Nur 52). Thus the verse gathers many meanings into concise and brief wording.

It is well known that concise expression is more difficult than elaboration and lengthiness. We have previously mentioned the story of the famous English orator, when they said to him: "If you were asked to prepare a speech to deliver in a quarter of an hour, how long would you take to prepare it?" He said: "A week." They said: "What if it were half an hour?" He said: "I would prepare it in two days." They said: "What if it were three hours?" He said: "I would prepare it now."

It is also said that Sa'd Pasha Zaghloul — may Allah have mercy on him — sent from France a letter to a friend, four pages long, in which he said: "As for what follows, I apologize to you for the lengthiness (elaboration), because I have no time for brevity."

(1) Al-Qurtubi mentioned in his tafsir (6/4833) that once Umar was standing in the Mosque of the Prophet (ﷺ) when a man of the Byzantine notables, with a cross on his head, was saying: "I bear witness that there is no god but Allah, and I bear witness that Muhammad is the Messenger of Allah." Umar said to him: "What is your situation?" He said: "I have embraced Islam for the sake of Allah." He said: "Is there a reason for this?" He said: "Yes. I have read the Torah, the Psalms, the Gospel and many books of the prophets, and I heard a captive reciting a verse of the Qur'an that gathers everything in the earlier books, so I knew that it was from Allah, and I embraced Islam." He said: "What is this verse?" He said: "The words of the Exalted: ﴿And whoever obeys Allah﴾ — in the obligations; ﴿and His Messenger﴾ — in the sunnah; ﴿and fears Allah﴾ — for what has passed of his life; ﴿and is mindful of Him﴾ — for what remains of his life; ﴿it is those who are the victorious﴾ — and the victorious is one who is saved from the Fire and admitted into Paradise." Umar said: The Prophet (ﷺ) said: "I have been given the comprehensive words (jawami' al-kalim)."

Commentary of al-Sha'rawi (Tafsir al-Sha'rawi, surahs 1-53, fragments of 54-66) on surah 24, verse 53:

After the Qur'an had spoken of the saying of the hypocrites, and of what stands in contrast to it, the saying of the believers, and the ruling that follows from it, ﴿Then those are the successful ones﴾ (al-Nur 52), this is because mentioning the opposite makes the opposite evident, as they say: "the opposite reveals the goodness of its opposite." After that it returned to speaking of hypocrisy and the hypocrites, and He, glorified is He, said:

﴿And they swore by Allah with their most emphatic oaths that if you ordered them, they would surely go forth. Say, "Do not swear; [what is required is] known obedience. Indeed, Allah is Acquainted with what you do."﴾ (al-Nur 53)

The qasam (oath) is the yamin (oath) and the halif (swearing). A person swears in order to confirm what he swears about; he wishes to reassure the listener that what he swears about is true. These people did not swear by Allah secretly within themselves, but rather {jahd aymanihim...} (al-Nur 53) means: they exaggerated and exerted the utmost effort in swearing. None of them said, "By the life of my mother or my father," but rather they swore by Allah, and there is no oath more emphatic than this oath. Therefore the Prophet (ﷺ) said: "Whoever is going to swear, let him swear by Allah, or let him keep silent."(1)

When they swore by Allah to the Messenger that they would go out from their homes, their children and their wealth to jihad with the Messenger of Allah, Allah exposed their inner secrets, uncovered their concealment, and made clear the falsity of their intentions, as He said in another verse: ﴿They say, "Obedience," but when they leave your presence, a faction of them spends the night devising other than what you say...﴾ (al-Nisa' 81).

Consider the precision of the Qur'anic expression in: ﴿a faction of them spends the night...﴾ (al-Nisa' 81). This is a measure of caution, because among them are people whose hearts are visited by faith and who consider purifying their faith and intentions for the sake of Allah, the Exalted, and returning to sound Islam.

The Qur'an exposes the affair of those who swear without sincerity in the oath, like one who is accustomed to frequent swearing and breaking oaths; therefore it forbids them from this swearing: ﴿Say, "Do not swear..."﴾ (al-Nur 53). It is not possible for the speaker to forbid the addressees from swearing, especially if they swear to something good, but these people break their oaths, so it is as if it did not exist; they swear with the tongue and contradict with the conscience.

His, the Exalted's, saying: ﴿[what is required is] known obedience...﴾ (al-Nur 53) implies rebuke of them, as if He were saying to them: "Your obedience is known to us, and it has clear precedents; it is obedience only with the tongue." Then He emphasizes this meaning, saying: ﴿Indeed, Allah is Acquainted with what you do﴾ (al-Nur 53). What confirms this knowledge is that He exposes their hearts and exposes their intentions.

Strangely, they do not take lessons from earlier events, nor are they admonished by them. It had already happened that one of them would sit and speak to himself, and Allah would expose what was in his soul and inform the Messenger of Allah, who would then tell them what was passing through their souls, as the saying of Allah, the Exalted, indicates: ﴿And they say within themselves, "Why does Allah not punish us for what we say?"...﴾ (al-Mujadila 8).

Nevertheless, they did not take heed, nor did they acknowledge to the Messenger of Allah that he is supported by Allah, and that He, the Exalted, will not abandon His Messenger or leave him to them to deceive and cheat him. These precedents recurred from them many times, and yet they did not desist from the hypocrisy they were engaged in, nor did they sincerely devote their faith to Allah.

(1) A hadith agreed upon (muttafaq 'alayh). It was narrated by al-Bukhari in his Sahih (2679, 3836, 6108) and likewise by Muslim in his Sahih (1646), in the Book of Oaths, from the hadith of Abdullah ibn Mas'ud. In Muslim's wording, Ibn Mas'ud came upon Umar ibn al-Khattab in a group while Umar was swearing by his father, so the Messenger of Allah (ﷺ) called out to them: "Verily Allah, Mighty and Majestic, forbids you to swear by your fathers. Whoever is going to swear, let him swear by Allah and keep silent."

Thereafter, after all of this, the Truth, blessed and exalted, enjoins upon His Prophet ﷺ that he should remain patient with them, and that he should not cast away (their clay, i.e., their lot) with "perhaps" and "maybe." So He, mighty and majestic, says:

﴿Say: Obey Allah and obey the Messenger. But if you turn away, then upon him is only what he has been charged with, and upon you is what you have been charged with. And if you obey him, you will be guided. And upon the Messenger is only the clear conveyance.﴾ [24:54]

It is as if He, exalted is He, does not wish to close the door upon them, so He gives them an opportunity: renew your obedience to Allah, renew your obedience to His Messenger, and make up for what has passed, for they are His servants and His creation.

And as has come in the noble hadith: "Allah is more delighted at the repentance of His servant than one of you who, having lost his mount in a desert wasteland, [then finds it]..." (1).

We note in this verse the repetition of the command "obey" — ﴿Obey Allah and obey the Messenger...﴾ [24:54] — whereas in other verses the command comes once, as in the preceding verse: ﴿And whoever obeys Allah and His Messenger...﴾ [24:52]; and in: ﴿Obey Allah and His Messenger...﴾ [8:20]; and in: ﴿Whoever obeys the Messenger has indeed obeyed Allah...﴾ [4:80]. That is: their obedience is one.

They said: Because the Qur'an is not merely a book of rulings, like the earlier scriptures; rather it is a book of inimitability (i'jaz), and its basic nature is that it is inimitable. Nevertheless, it included some foundations and rulings, and left others for the Messenger's explanation and clarification in the noble hadith. He ﷺ was given a right in legislation by the explicit text of the Qur'an: ﴿And whatever the Messenger gives you, take it; and whatever he forbids you, refrain from it...﴾ [59:7].

When the Qur'an presents rulings, it presents them in summary, and then the Messenger of Allah ﷺ elaborates them. Prayer, for example, Allah the Truth, blessed and exalted, enjoined and made obligatory; but its details came in the purified Sunnah of the Prophet. For He said: "If you want the details, then consult the Sunnah."

It is like one who says: if an employee is absent from his work for fifteen days, he is subject to elaboration (dismissal), though the constitution did not state this. We say: but in the constitution there is a specific article for employees that regulates such matters and lays down the regulations governing work.

We mentioned that Shaykh Muhammad 'Abduh was asked by some Orientalists: You say in the Qur'an: ﴿We have neglected nothing in the Book...﴾ [6:38]. So bring me from the Qur'an: how many loaves are in an ardab of wheat? The Shaykh did nothing but send for a baker and ask him this question, and he answered: in the ardab there are such-and-such loaves. The questioner objected: I want it from the Qur'an.

The Shaykh replied: This is from the Qur'an, for He says: ﴿So ask the people of remembrance if you do not know﴾ [16:43].

So a matter in which a ruling comes from Allah and a ruling from the Messenger of Allah — such as prayer, for example: ﴿Indeed, prayer has been enjoined upon the believers at fixed times﴾ [4:103].

And in the hadith: "Prayer is the pillar of the religion" (2).

So in such a matter we say: obey Allah and the Messenger, for both bear upon a single matter, so the command to obey came as one.

As for matters of the number of units (rak'ahs), what is recited in each unit, and whether it is recited silently or aloud — these are all matters the Messenger of Allah clarified. Thus there is obedience to Allah in the general legislation, that prayer is obligatory, and there is obedience specific to the Messenger in the detailed elaboration of this legislation; therefore the command comes twice: ﴿Obey Allah and obey the Messenger...﴾ [24:54].

Likewise we observe in the Qur'an: ﴿And obey the Messenger...﴾ [24:56], just like this, alone.

They said: this is in matters for which no legislation or explicit text was given; the Messenger, in that case, is the legislator. This is among the distinctions of the Prophet ﷺ over all the messengers, for they all came to receive legislation and convey it to the people, whereas he ﷺ was the only one entrusted by Allah with legislation.

Then He, exalted is He, says: ﴿But if they turn away, then upon him is only what he has been charged with, and upon you is what you have been charged with...﴾ [24:54]. This is because He, exalted is He, knows the eagerness of the Prophet for the guidance of the people, and how he exerts himself in calling them, as He addressed him elsewhere: ﴿Perhaps you would kill yourself with grief that they will not be believers﴾ [26:3]. As if the Truth, blessed and exalted, says to His Prophet: Say to them, and call them a second time, to relieve yourself — ﴿Say: Obey Allah and obey the Messenger...﴾ [24:54]. And although you are not obligated to repetition, your only duty is to convey once.

The meaning of ﴿...then upon him is only what he has been charged with, and upon you is what you have been charged with...﴾ [24:54] is: that is, from Allah. The Messenger bore the call and the conveyance, and you bear the obedience and the fulfilment; so it is upon you to perform what Allah has charged you with.

﴿And if you obey him, you will be guided...﴾ [24:54]: We note that the object in ﴿if you obey him...﴾ [24:54] is singular. He did not say "obey them both," so as to match the opening of the verse ﴿Obey Allah and obey the Messenger...﴾ [24:54]. This is because obedience here is not divided, but is one single obedience.

As for His saying ﴿And upon the Messenger is only the clear conveyance﴾ [24:54], it is an obligation laid upon him by Allah: the conveyance that is clear, encompassing every detail of the legislative method for organizing the movement of life.

1. A hadith agreed upon (muttafaq 'alayh). Recorded by al-Bukhari in his Sahih (6308–6309), and likewise by Muslim in his Sahih (2744), from the hadith of 'Abdullah ibn Mas'ud. Al-falah: the vast desert that is barren of crops and vegetation.
2. The complete hadith: "Whoever establishes it has established the religion, and whoever abandons it has demolished the religion." al-Hafiz al-'Iraqi said in his takhrij of the hadiths of the Ihya' (1/147): "al-Bayhaqi narrated it in al-Shu'ab with a weak chain, from the hadith of 'Umar." Mulla 'Ali al-Qari said in al-Asrar al-Marfu'ah (hadith 578): "Ibn al-Salah said in Mushkil al-Wasit: 'It is not known.'" And al-Suyuti mentioned it in al-Durar al-Muntathirah (no. 279).

Then Allah, glorified is He, says:

﴿Allah has promised those of you who believe and do righteous deeds that He will surely make them successors upon the earth, just as He made successors those before them, and that He will surely establish for them their religion which He has approved for them, and that He will surely replace their fear with security, [saying], "They worship Me, not associating anything with Me. And whoever disbelieves after that, those are the defiantly disobedient."﴾

At the beginning of our discussion of Surah al-Nur, we said that it was named "al-Nur" (the Light) because it explains to people the sensory light in the universe and draws an analogy from it to the moral light in values. Since we extinguish our sensory lights when the light of Allah appears in the sun, we must likewise extinguish our moral lights when a law (shar') comes to us from Allah.

There is no opinion [that can stand] alongside the law of Allah. This is because the Creator, Mighty and Majestic, wants His vicegerent on earth to be in sensory and moral light. Then He guaranteed for him the means of sustaining his life through food and drink, on condition that it be lawful (halal), so that his cells are built and formed from what is lawful, and thus his receiving apparatus from Allah remains sound, and his sending apparatus (for supplication) too, if he wishes to call upon Him.

In the noble hadith: "O people, Allah is Pure and accepts only what is pure, and Allah has commanded the believers with what He commanded the messengers. He said: ﴿O messengers, eat of the good things and do righteousness; indeed, I am Knowing of what you do﴾ [al-Mu'minun: 51], and He said: ﴿O you who have believed, eat of the good things We have provided you...﴾ [al-Baqarah: 172]." Then he mentioned a man who prolongs the journey, disheveled and dusty, raising his hands to the sky, saying, "O Lord, O Lord," while his food is unlawful, his drink is unlawful, his clothing is unlawful, and he is nourished by the unlawful: how then could he be answered?" (2)

These are disabled, ruined receivers, much like a radio that does not properly receive what the broadcasting stations transmit: the transmission is ongoing and others receive it, but as for him, his receiver is not sound.

So if you secure the soundness of your constitution through a morsel of the lawful, Allah guarantees you the answering of supplication. In a hadith, the Prophet (ﷺ) said to Sa'd ibn Abi Waqqas (may Allah be pleased with him): "Make your food pure, and you will be one whose supplication is answered." (3)

Then Allah guaranteed to humankind the means of preserving its species through marriage, for the continuation of offspring, so that the vicegerency on earth continues pure and clean. Then the Surah addressed, warning you not to presume upon people's honour, nor to accuse chaste women, nor to enter houses without seeking permission, lest you look upon people's nakedness... etc.

Allah, Blessed and Exalted, desires the safety of society and the safety of the vicegerency on earth, and all these rulings and meanings flow into this verse:

﴿Allah has promised those of you who believe and do righteous deeds that He will surely make them successors upon the earth...﴾ [al-Nur: 55]. Whoever does that is worthy of vicegerency from Allah. It is a struggle of trials and purification that distinguishes the worthless (ghath) (4) from the good. Do you not see how the early Muslims were tortured and persecuted, and no one dared to protect them, until they were forced to emigrate to Abyssinia and to Medina? Allah, Exalted, has said: ﴿Do people think they will be left alone because they say, "We believe," and they will not be tested?﴾ [al-'Ankabut: 2].

These Companions are the ones who carried the torches of guidance to the world and travelled far and wide with Allah's call throughout the earth. They had to be raised in this harsh discipline and tested with this severe trial, knowing well the price of this sacrifice and awaiting its reward from Allah. The people of truth pay the price first, whereas the people of false principles collect the price first before they move in the direction of their principles. This trial that the early Muslims endured was part of purifying the vicegerent so that he would be worthy of it.

Therefore He, glorified is He, said: ﴿Allah has promised... [al-Nur: 55]. Al-wa'd (promise) is good news of something whose time has not yet come, so that people may prepare the means for it; its opposite is al-wa'id (threat) or warning of evil, a evil whose time has not yet come, so that there is an opportunity for precaution and avoiding falling into its causes.

Since the promise is from Allah, Exalted, it is true, as He, glorified is He, said: ﴿And who is more truthful in speech than Allah?﴾ [al-Nisa': 122], and He, glorified is He, said: ﴿And who is more faithful to his covenant than Allah?﴾ [al-Tawbah: 111].

What spoils people's promises and brings about their non-fulfilment is that man is changeable by nature, fickle. He may promise a person good, then his heart changes toward him and he does not fulfil what he promised; or the time of fulfilment comes and he is unable to do it. As for the Real, blessed and exalted, He never changes, and He, glorified is He, is able to fulfil what He has promised; there is no other power that prevents Him. He, glorified is He, is One, there is no god other than Him; therefore His promise, exalted is He, is immediate.

﴿Allah has promised those of you who believe and do righteous deeds...﴾ [al-Nur: 55]. We have said that faith which rests upon the purity of the spring and the creed is not sought for its own sake; rather it must bear fruit, and its effect must be seen as obedience and execution of Allah's commands. As long as you believe in Allah, carry out what He commands you. There are people who do good, but not from a basis of faith, like the hypocrites about whom Allah said: ﴿The Bedouins say, "We have believed." ... [al-Hujurat: 14]. Allah answered them: ﴿Say, "You have not believed; but say, 'We have submitted'..."﴾ [al-Hujurat: 14], meaning: we have submitted to the commands, but without faith. So the value of faith is that you carry out what it requires.

Among this is also His saying, Exalted: ﴿By time, indeed mankind is in loss, except for those who have believed and done righteous deeds and advised one another to truth and advised one another to patience﴾ [al-'Asr: 1-3].

So with what did Allah promise those who believe? ﴿That He will surely make them successors upon the earth...﴾ [al-Nur: 55]. This is not new: those before them, their predecessors, had gone before them: ﴿just as He made successors those before them...﴾ [al-Nur: 55]. So the successorship of those who believe is not novel; rather it is a matter witnessed in the processions of the messengers and prophethood, and witnessed among the early Muslim Companions who were harmed, tortured, persecuted, and expelled from their homes, their children and their wealth, and were not commanded to repel aggression.

Indeed, when the Messenger of Allah (ﷺ) arrived in Medina with a group of his Companions, the Ansar welcomed him warmly and embraced these emigrants, and they showed toward them a model of selflessness unmatched in the history of humanity. Is there any greater selflessness than that an Ansari would offer his wives to the emigrant, saying, "Choose one of them, and I will divorce her for you"? To this degree did faith affect the souls of the Ansar.

When the disbelievers of Quraysh saw what the Ansar had done for the emigrants, they blazed with fire: how could the emigrants live this pleasant life in Medina? They united all together against this religion to strike it with one bow, and they conspired against its leader in order to destroy this nascent religion, which posed the greatest danger to them.

So much so that the emigrants and the Ansar reached the point that they would not spend the night except with weapons, nor would they rise in the morning except with weapons, fearing that their enemies would pounce upon them. To the extent that one of the Companions said to his brothers: "Do you think we will live to be secure and at peace, not spending the night or rising in the morning with weapons, fearing none but Allah?" meaning: is there any hope for this goal?

Another went to the Messenger of Allah (ﷺ) and said: "O Messenger of Allah, shall we be fearful forever? Will there not come to us, will there not come to us, a day when we lay down our weapons and spend the night in safety?"

The Prophet (ﷺ) replied in the tone of one confident of his Lord's promise, not words that might be falsified later: "You will not wait but a little while until a man among you sits in the great assembly, sitting comfortably (muhtabiyan), with no iron (weapon) in it." meaning: in the wide gathering. Ihtiba' is the posture of one at rest and at ease, and "iron" is a metaphor for weapons.

He (ﷺ) also said: "Indeed Allah gathered the earth for me, so I saw its easts and its wests, and the dominion of my community will reach what was gathered for me of it." (6)

The meaning of "Allah gathered the earth for me" is that it is known that a person has a field of vision which extends to the horizon, whereas the earth itself is vast; so the earth was gathered for the Messenger of Allah, meaning it was brought together into a corner, so that he could see all of it.

So in this stage they longed for security and tranquility of mind. Allah, Exalted, said of them in this period: ﴿And they were shaken until the Messenger and those who believed with him said, "When is the help of Allah?"﴾ [al-Baqarah: 214].

In the midst of this hardship and the height of this straitness, Allah, Exalted, revealed to His Messenger: ﴿The multitude will be put to flight and will turn their backs﴾ [al-Qamar: 45]. So much so that the Companions were astonished. 'Umar (may Allah be pleased with him) said: "What multitude is this?" The verse had been revealed while they were in Mecca in intense fear, unable to protect themselves.

But after Badr, and after he saw what had befallen the disbelievers, he said: "Allah has spoken truly: ﴿The multitude will be put to flight and will turn their backs﴾ [al-Qamar: 45]."

Then Allah, Exalted, revealed to His Messenger (ﷺ) some verses that reassure and steady the believers: ﴿Do they not see that We come to the land, reducing it from its outskirts? And Allah judges; there is no repeller of His judgment...﴾ [al-Ra'd: 41].

So be reassured: every day We reduce the land of disbelief and increase the land of faith, so the preliminaries are in your favour. Then came the conquest of Mecca, and the Prophet (ﷺ) entered it in a majestic procession, lowering his head in humility toward the One who admitted him, manifesting the submissiveness of servanthood to Allah.

So much so that when Abu Sufyan saw the Messenger of Allah (ﷺ) in this procession, he said to al-'Abbas: "The kingdom of your nephew has become great." Al-'Abbas said: "It is prophethood, O Abu Sufyan." (7) meaning: the matter is not kingship; rather these are the tidings of victory for the religion of Allah and its dominance over the stronghold of idols and images in Mecca.

Then he went to Khaybar, the stronghold of the People of the Book from Banu Qaynuqa', Banu al-Nadir and Banu Qurayzah, and gained victory over them. Then the Bahrain and the Magians of Hajar fell into his hand, and they paid the jizyah.

After that, he (ﷺ) sent his letters to kings and chiefs inviting them to Islam: he sent to the Negus, king of Abyssinia, to al-Muqawqis, to Heraclius, and to Khosrow, and gifts came to him from all of them.

The Islamic expansion continued, and the fulfilment of Allah's promise to the successor of the Messenger of Allah: if the Islamic expansion had covered the Arabian Peninsula during the time of the Messenger of Allah, it went beyond it to the various regions of the world during the time of the Rightly Guided Caliphs, until Islam prevailed over the whole world, and Allah made it dominant over the two greatest civilisations of that time: the civilisation of Persia in the East and the civilisation of Rome in the West, at one and the same time. Thus Allah's promise to those who believe, that He would make them successors on the earth, was realised.

After the death of the Messenger of Allah (ﷺ), the prophecies he had foretold came to pass, among them what happened with Suraqah ibn Malik, who set out after the Messenger of Allah during the migration, seeking to capture him and win the reward of Quraysh. After Suraqah repented and returned to the right path, the Companions would marvel at the thickness of his forearms and describe them in a way that provoked laughter, and the Prophet (ﷺ) said of Suraqah's forearms: "How will you be with them in the bracelets of Khosrow?" (8)

Then the Muslims conquered the kingdom of Khosrow, and the two bracelets of Khosrow became Suraqah's portion; he wore them, and people saw them on his hands.

All these are tidings and preliminaries to Allah's promise, which the believers see in themselves, not in those who come after: ﴿Allah has promised those of you who believe...﴾ [al-Nur: 55]. That is: the matter will not be long.

Likewise Umm Haram bint Milhan (9), who went out in the expedition of the masts and boarded the sea, mentioned that the Messenger of Allah (ﷺ) used to sleep there and then wake up laughing. She said to him: "What makes you laugh, O Messenger of Allah?" He said: "Some people of my community will ride the foam of this sea, kings on thrones, or like kings on thrones." She said: "Pray to Allah that I may be among them." He prayed for her, and Allah answered his prayer. She went out in the expedition, and when they boarded the White Sea (Mediterranean), she wanted to disembark and died. (10)

So the good tidings in this verse are not verbal tidings; rather they are realistic tidings that have a reality that fulfils them, which has indeed happened.

But what is meant by "the earth" in ﴿He will surely make them successors upon the earth...﴾ [al-Nur: 55]? When "the earth" comes in this manner, singular and not annexed to anything, it means the whole earth, as in His saying: ﴿And We said after him to the Children of Israel, "Dwell in the land..."﴾ [al-Isra': 104], meaning: you will be scattered throughout all its regions; ﴿So when the promise of the Hereafter comes...﴾ [al-Isra': 104], which Allah promised...
